preguntas.q: Ovarian surface epithelial tumors generally have a poor prognosis largely because of which characteristic clinical feature?

o.C: Late presentation due to vague/nonspecific symptoms

e.correcta: Ovarian surface epithelial tumors, particularly malignant ones, often produce only vague, nonspecific symptoms (bloating, pelvic discomfort, early satiety) because the ovary sits deep in the pelvis with room for a mass to grow substantially before causing pressure symptoms or being palpable; as a result, most cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage (often after peritoneal spread) when treatment is less effective, which is the primary reason ovarian cancer overall carries a comparatively poor prognosis.

incorrectas.A: Rapid hematogenous spread to bone is not the typical behavior of ovarian surface epithelial tumors, which more characteristically spread by direct extension and transcoelomic seeding across peritoneal surfaces rather than through the bloodstream to bone.
incorrectas.B: Early, easily detected symptoms is the opposite of what actually happens — the vague, nonspecific nature of early symptoms (rather than clear early warning signs) is precisely why these tumors are typically found late.
incorrectas.D: Universal chemoresistance is inaccurate; many ovarian epithelial carcinomas are initially quite chemosensitive (e.g., to platinum-based regimens), and the poor overall prognosis is driven mainly by late-stage diagnosis rather than inherent resistance to all chemotherapy.

preguntas.q: Ovarian surface epithelial tumors typically present with vague abdominal pain/fullness along with which additional symptom reflecting local mass effect?

e.correcta: Ovarian surface epithelial tumors often grow silently until they become large enough to exert mass effect on adjacent pelvic structures, and because the bladder lies immediately anterior to the ovaries/uterus, urinary frequency from direct bladder compression is a common accompanying symptom alongside vague abdominal fullness or bloating. This nonspecific presentation is part of why ovarian cancer is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage, since early symptoms are easily mistaken for benign gastrointestinal or urinary complaints.

incorrectas.A: Hematuria from bladder invasion would imply direct tumor infiltration through the bladder wall, a late and less typical finding, whereas the more characteristic early mass-effect symptom is simple compression causing urinary frequency, not invasion causing bleeding.
incorrectas.C: Hematochezia from rectal invasion similarly implies direct tumor invasion into the bowel, which is not the classic early presenting symptom; vague fullness plus bladder compression symptoms are more typical initial complaints.
incorrectas.D: Galactorrhea is related to hyperprolactinemia (e.g., from a prolactinoma) and has no connection to mass effect from an ovarian tumor, making it inconsistent with the local compressive symptoms described in the question.

preguntas.q: Which serum tumor marker is used to monitor treatment response and detect recurrence in ovarian surface epithelial neoplasms, despite being unreliable for screening?

e.correcta: CA-125 is a glycoprotein antigen expressed by many surface epithelial ovarian tumors (especially serous carcinomas) that can be measured serially; because its level generally correlates with tumor burden, falling levels after treatment support a good response and rising levels can signal recurrence before it is clinically apparent. It performs poorly as a general population screening test because it lacks sensitivity for early-stage disease and lacks specificity (it is also elevated in benign conditions like endometriosis, fibroids, and pelvic inflammatory disease), so its clinical utility is confined to monitoring known disease rather than screening asymptomatic women.

incorrectas.A: AFP (alpha-fetoprotein) is the tumor marker associated with yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumors and hepatocellular carcinoma, not with surface epithelial ovarian neoplasms, so it is not used to monitor this tumor category.
incorrectas.C: hCG is elevated in choriocarcinoma and some mixed germ cell tumors, reflecting trophoblastic differentiation, and is not the marker used for surface epithelial tumors like serous or mucinous carcinoma.
incorrectas.D: CA 19-9 is more classically associated with pancreatic and biliary tract cancers (and can be elevated in mucinous ovarian tumors to some degree), but it is not the standard marker used for monitoring surface epithelial ovarian neoplasms in general the way CA-125 is.

preguntas.q: Which category of ovarian tumor is the second most common overall, accounting for roughly 15% of ovarian tumors?

e.correcta: Germ cell tumors of the ovary (including mature teratomas/dermoid cysts, dysgerminomas, and yolk sac tumors) make up roughly 15% of ovarian tumors, making them the second most common category behind surface epithelial tumors, which dominate overall ovarian tumor incidence. Germ cell tumors are notably more common in younger women and children, in contrast to epithelial tumors, which are more typical in older, postmenopausal women.

incorrectas.A: Sex cord-stromal tumors (such as granulosa cell tumors and Sertoli-Leydig tumors) are a less common category overall, often notable for hormone production (estrogen or androgen), but they do not reach the roughly 15% share held by germ cell tumors.
incorrectas.B: Surface epithelial tumors are actually the most common ovarian tumor category overall (including serous and mucinous cystadenomas/carcinomas), not the second most common, so this does not match the 15% figure described in the question.
incorrectas.D: Metastatic tumors to the ovary (e.g., Krukenberg tumors from GI primaries) are an important but less frequent category, and are not classically cited as accounting for the second-largest share of ovarian tumors.

preguntas.q: Ovarian germ cell tumors most commonly affect which demographic, in contrast to surface epithelial tumors which occur in older women?

o.B: Women of reproductive age, 15-30 years old

e.correcta: Ovarian germ cell tumors (such as dysgerminoma, teratoma, and yolk sac tumor) most commonly arise in women of reproductive age, roughly 15-30 years old, because they originate from the primordial germ cells that are most actively present and proliferating during this life stage. This contrasts with surface epithelial ovarian tumors (like serous and mucinous cystadenocarcinomas), which arise from the ovarian surface epithelium and predominantly affect older, typically postmenopausal women, reflecting a different cell of origin and different age-related risk pattern.

incorrectas.A: Postmenopausal women aged 60-70 are the classic demographic for surface epithelial ovarian tumors, which is the contrasting group specifically mentioned in the question stem, not the demographic for germ cell tumors.
incorrectas.C: Perimenopausal women aged 45-55 fall between the two classic peaks described (reproductive-age germ cell tumors and postmenopausal epithelial tumors) and are not the demographic characteristically associated with germ cell tumors.
incorrectas.D: Prepubertal girls under age 10 can rarely develop germ cell tumors, but the peak incidence classically taught for ovarian germ cell tumors is in the reproductive age range (15-30), not this younger prepubertal group.

preguntas.q: An ovarian cystic mass contains hair, teeth, bone, and skin, representing tissue derived from two or three embryologic germ layers. What is this tumor?

e.correcta: A cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is a germ cell tumor arising from a totipotent germ cell that undergoes parthenogenetic-like differentiation into tissues from multiple embryologic germ layers (ectoderm, and often mesoderm and/or endoderm), which is why it characteristically contains skin, hair, teeth, sebaceous material, and sometimes cartilage or bone within a cystic cavity. This multi-germ-layer differentiation, arising from a single totipotent cell, is the defining feature that distinguishes teratomas from other germ cell tumors that differentiate along a single lineage.

incorrectas.A: Dysgerminoma is composed of undifferentiated, primitive germ cells resembling primordial oocytes (analogous to seminoma) and does not differentiate into mature tissues like hair, teeth, or skin — it remains a solid tumor of uniform undifferentiated cells rather than a multi-tissue cystic mass.
incorrectas.C: Endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor differentiates to recapitulate extraembryonic yolk sac tissue and characteristically secretes AFP, but it does not contain mature ectodermal/mesodermal derivatives like hair, teeth, or skin.
incorrectas.D: Choriocarcinoma differentiates along trophoblastic lines (cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast), secreting hCG, and is a hemorrhagic, necrotic solid tumor rather than a cyst containing mature tissue from multiple germ layers.

preguntas.q: In females aged 10-30, which is the most common germ cell tumor of the ovary, bilateral in about 10% of cases?

e.correcta: Cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is the most common germ cell tumor of the ovary in the 10-30 year age range, reflecting the fact that germ cell tumors as a category predominate in younger women (in contrast to surface epithelial tumors, which trend older); its bilaterality rate of about 10% is a distinguishing feature useful for surgical planning, since a contralateral ovary should be inspected/preserved when feasible in a young patient wishing to maintain fertility.

incorrectas.A: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant germ cell tumor in this age group, but it is considerably less common overall than the benign cystic teratoma when considering all germ cell tumors together, so it is not the single most common germ cell tumor type.
incorrectas.B: Embryonal carcinoma is a rare, highly aggressive germ cell tumor that occurs much less frequently than cystic teratoma in this age range and does not share its characteristic ~10% bilaterality rate.
incorrectas.D: Endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor is an AFP-secreting germ cell tumor typically seen in young children/adolescents, but it is far less common overall than cystic teratoma across the 10-30 age range.

preguntas.q: What is the malignant potential of a mature cystic teratoma of the ovary?

e.correcta: Mature cystic teratomas are composed of fully differentiated, adult-type tissues (skin, hair, teeth, etc.) arranged in an organized, non-invasive fashion, which is why the overwhelming majority behave in a purely benign fashion with essentially no risk of local invasion or metastasis. Malignant transformation (most often to squamous cell carcinoma arising from the skin component) is a rare but recognized late complication, typically in older patients with long-standing teratomas, but this does not change the fundamentally benign nature of the tumor itself.

incorrectas.A: Uniformly malignant describes the opposite of a mature cystic teratoma's actual behavior; it is the immature teratoma (containing embryonic/fetal-type tissue, notably immature neuroepithelium) that carries malignant potential, not the mature, fully differentiated variant.
incorrectas.C: Borderline malignant potential is a category reserved for certain epithelial tumors with atypia but no invasion (e.g., borderline serous tumors), not a designation applied to mature cystic teratomas, which are considered benign rather than existing on a borderline spectrum.
incorrectas.D: Always metastatic at diagnosis is inaccurate and essentially the inverse of reality; mature cystic teratomas are overwhelmingly benign and localized, with metastatic or malignant behavior being a rare exception rather than the rule.

preguntas.q: What is the malignant potential of an immature ovarian teratoma?

e.correcta: Immature ovarian teratomas contain embryonic-appearing (immature) neuroectodermal tissue, and unlike the mature/dermoid cystic teratoma, they behave as malignant germ cell tumors capable of local invasion and metastasis. Grading is based on the amount of immature neural tissue present, which correlates with prognosis, but any amount of immature tissue confers real malignant potential, so this tumor cannot be assumed benign the way a mature teratoma can. This distinction (mature = benign, immature = malignant) is one of the most heavily tested points about ovarian teratomas.

incorrectas.A: Mature cystic teratomas (dermoid cysts) are the ones that are almost always benign; calling the immature variant 'always benign' ignores the defining feature that separates it from its mature counterpart, which is precisely the presence of malignant immature elements.
incorrectas.C: Immature teratomas are actually defined by containing immature neuroectodermal (neural) tissue — that is the hallmark finding used for diagnosis and grading, so stating they never contain neural tissue is the opposite of the truth.
incorrectas.D: Malignant potential in immature teratomas is determined by the grade of immature tissue present, not by whether the tumor is bilateral; bilaterality is not the criterion used to assess malignancy in germ cell tumors of this type.

preguntas.q: Which fetal tissue type is most commonly responsible for malignancy in an immature ovarian teratoma?

e.correcta: In immature ovarian teratomas, malignancy is defined by the presence and amount of immature neuroectodermal tissue (primitive neuroepithelial rosettes and tubules resembling fetal neural tube), which is the tissue component graded to determine tumor grade and prognosis. Unlike mature (benign) teratomas that contain fully differentiated tissues from all three germ layers, immature teratomas contain embryonic-appearing tissue capable of aggressive growth and metastasis, and the amount of immature neural tissue per slide is precisely what pathologists quantify for grading. This is why neuroectoderm — not cartilage, skin, or gut — is the tissue that drives the malignant potential.

incorrectas.A: Immature cartilage can be present in a teratoma but is not the tissue used to assess malignant grade; cartilage differentiation, even if immature-appearing, does not carry the same aggressive biological behavior as immature neuroectoderm.
incorrectas.B: Immature skin (ectodermal derivatives forming epidermis and adnexal structures) is a common component of teratomas but, like cartilage, is not the tissue whose quantity defines tumor grade or malignant potential.
incorrectas.D: Immature gut epithelium represents endodermal differentiation within the teratoma and, similar to the other distractors, is not the histologic feature used to grade malignancy — that role is specifically reserved for immature neuroectodermal tissue.

preguntas.q: Beyond containing immature tissue, cystic teratomas can also become malignant through which additional mechanism?

o.B: Somatic malignant transformation of a mature tissue component

e.correcta: Even a histologically mature (benign-appearing) cystic teratoma can rarely undergo malignant transformation of one of its differentiated tissue components, most classically squamous cell carcinoma arising from the skin/squamous epithelium lining the cyst. This is a distinct mechanism from immaturity itself — the tumor is fully differentiated but one of its mature elements acquires additional somatic mutations and becomes a true invasive cancer, usually in older women and often presenting as a rapidly enlarging mass.

incorrectas.A: Germline BRCA mutations predispose to epithelial ovarian and breast cancers, not to malignant transformation of a teratoma's tissue components; teratoma pathogenesis is not linked to BRCA status.
incorrectas.C: Loss of imprinting is a mechanism implicated in conditions like Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome and some tumors of imprinted loci, but it is not the recognized pathway by which mature teratoma components become malignant.
incorrectas.D: t(11;22) is the classic translocation of Ewing sarcoma, an unrelated small round blue cell tumor of bone/soft tissue, and has no role in teratoma malignant transformation.

preguntas.q: When a cystic teratoma undergoes somatic malignant transformation, which cancer type most commonly arises?

e.correcta: Mature cystic teratomas (dermoid cysts) contain tissue from all three germ layers, and the ectodermal component (skin and skin appendages) is the most abundant tissue type, so when malignant transformation occurs it most often produces squamous cell carcinoma arising from this predominant squamous/epidermal element. This is a classically tested complication of an otherwise benign and common ovarian tumor, usually occurring in older women with a long-standing teratoma.

incorrectas.A: Thyroid tissue can be present in a teratoma (struma ovarii) and can rarely become malignant, but this is a much less common transformation than squamous cell carcinoma arising from the dominant ectodermal/skin component.
incorrectas.C: Small cell carcinoma is not the characteristic malignant transformation of a mature cystic teratoma; it is not the predominant tissue type within these tumors.
incorrectas.D: Osteosarcoma would require a bone tissue component to transform malignantly, but bone is not the predominant tissue type in a teratoma, unlike skin/squamous epithelium, making squamous cell carcinoma far more common.

preguntas.q: What is the most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary in females, accounting for about 30% of germ cell tumors?

e.correcta: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary, accounting for roughly 30% of ovarian germ cell malignancies, composed of large cells with clear cytoplasm and central nuclei resembling primordial germ cells (histologically identical to testicular seminoma), and is notably radiosensitive with generally excellent prognosis when treated. It classically occurs in adolescents/young women and can elevate serum LDH, making it a useful tumor marker to follow.

incorrectas.A: Choriocarcinoma is a highly aggressive germ cell tumor that secretes beta-hCG and can arise from gestational or germ cell origin, but it is considerably less common than dysgerminoma among ovarian germ cell tumors and tends to metastasize hematogenously early.
incorrectas.B: Embryonal carcinoma is a more aggressive, less differentiated germ cell tumor that can secrete both AFP and hCG, but it occurs less frequently than dysgerminoma and is not the 30%-prevalence tumor described here.
incorrectas.C: Endodermal sinus tumor (yolk sac tumor) is characterized by Schiller-Duval bodies and elevated AFP, typically seen in younger children, but it is not the most common ovarian germ cell malignancy — that distinction belongs to dysgerminoma.

preguntas.q: Ovarian dysgerminoma is the histologic and biologic equivalent of which testicular germ cell tumor in males?

e.correcta: Ovarian dysgerminoma and testicular seminoma arise from the same undifferentiated germ cell lineage and share identical histology (sheets of large cells with clear cytoplasm and central nuclei, admixed with lymphocytes), identical exquisite radiosensitivity, and an excellent prognosis, differing only by the organ of origin and sex. This male-female histologic pairing is a frequently tested correspondence in germ cell tumor pathology.

incorrectas.A: Embryonal carcinoma is a distinct, more aggressive undifferentiated germ cell tumor found in the testis; its ovarian counterpart would not be dysgerminoma, which instead corresponds specifically to seminoma.
incorrectas.B: Yolk sac tumor is the counterpart tumor type that occurs in both testis and ovary bearing the same name and AFP-secreting behavior, but it is a distinct entity from dysgerminoma/seminoma, which is defined by its own seminoma-like histology.
incorrectas.D: Choriocarcinoma, whether ovarian or testicular, arises from trophoblastic differentiation and secretes hCG, representing yet another distinct germ cell tumor category unrelated to the dysgerminoma-seminoma pairing.

preguntas.q: What is the general prognosis of ovarian dysgerminoma, given its responsiveness to radiotherapy?

o.D: Prognosis is unpredictable and unrelated to treatment

e.correcta: Dysgerminoma, the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma, is composed of uniform primitive germ cells that are exquisitely radiosensitive, so even when the tumor has spread beyond the ovary, radiotherapy (and chemotherapy) achieves excellent response rates and long-term survival. This favorable prognosis, despite dysgerminoma being malignant, is a key teaching point distinguishing it from more aggressive, chemoresistant germ cell tumors.

incorrectas.A: While dysgerminoma can spread to lymph nodes, its overall behavior is not one of rapid fulminant metastasis with poor outcomes — its radiosensitivity instead confers a good prognosis, contradicting this option.
incorrectas.C: Dysgerminoma is not uniformly fatal; because of its high sensitivity to radiation and chemotherapy, most patients achieve long-term cure, making 'uniformly fatal within a year' inaccurate.
incorrectas.D: The prognosis is not unpredictable — it correlates directly with the tumor's known radiosensitivity, giving it a consistently favorable outcome with appropriate treatment rather than an unrelated or random course.

preguntas.q: Which two serum markers may be elevated in a patient with ovarian dysgerminoma?

e.correcta: Dysgerminoma, the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma, is composed of primitive germ cells with high glycolytic activity, which explains the elevated serum LDH frequently seen; a subset of these tumors also contain scattered syncytiotrophoblastic giant cells that secrete hCG, causing mild elevation of that marker as well. Recognizing this LDH/hCG pattern helps distinguish dysgerminoma from other germ cell tumors that have their own characteristic markers (like AFP in yolk sac tumor).

incorrectas.A: AFP is the marker for yolk sac tumor, and CA-125 is a nonspecific marker of epithelial ovarian tumors—neither is the classic marker pairing for dysgerminoma, which instead is associated with LDH and sometimes hCG.
incorrectas.B: hCG can be mildly elevated in dysgerminoma due to syncytiotrophoblastic giant cells, but CA 19-9 is not a typical marker for this tumor; the paired marker classically taught alongside hCG for dysgerminoma is LDH, not CA 19-9.
incorrectas.D: AFP is not produced by dysgerminoma (that is characteristic of yolk sac tumor or mixed germ cell tumors with a yolk sac component), so pairing it with LDH does not reflect the actual marker profile of pure dysgerminoma.

preguntas.q: Ovarian dysgerminoma is most commonly diagnosed in which patient population?

e.correcta: Ovarian dysgerminoma, the female counterpart of testicular seminoma, arises from primordial germ cells and typically occurs in adolescent and young adult females, often presenting as a unilateral solid ovarian mass. Like seminoma, it is composed of sheets of large cells with clear cytoplasm and central nuclei, is exquisitely radiosensitive, and carries an excellent prognosis with appropriate treatment. Recognizing the age distribution helps distinguish it from epithelial ovarian tumors, which predominate in older women.

incorrectas.A: Postmenopausal women are the classic population for epithelial ovarian tumors (e.g., serous or mucinous cystadenocarcinoma), not germ cell tumors like dysgerminoma, which arise from germ cells still active during the reproductive years of youth.
incorrectas.C: Prepubertal children under age 5 are more typically associated with yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumors, which produce AFP, rather than dysgerminoma, which peaks slightly later in adolescence and young adulthood.
incorrectas.D: Women in their 40s and 50s are more at risk for epithelial ovarian neoplasms as surface epithelial inclusion cysts accumulate genetic damage over time, a different tumor lineage and age pattern than the germ-cell-derived dysgerminoma.

preguntas.q: Which germ cell tumor is the most common cause of ovarian or testicular malignancy in young children, especially male infants, and can also arise in the sacrococcygeal area?

e.correcta: The endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor is the most common germ cell malignancy in infants and young children, arising in the ovary, testis, or extragonadally in the sacrococcygeal region because it recapitulates yolk sac (extraembryonic endoderm) differentiation, which is prominent very early in development. It secretes AFP, making serum AFP a useful tumor marker for diagnosis and monitoring, and its characteristic histology (Schiller-Duval bodies) reflects this yolk sac lineage.

incorrectas.A: Dysgerminoma/seminoma is the most common germ cell tumor overall in adolescents and young adults (not infants), and while malignant, it is not the classic pediatric/infantile tumor with sacrococcygeal presentation described here.
incorrectas.B: Choriocarcinoma is a highly aggressive trophoblastic germ cell tumor that secretes beta-hCG and spreads hematogenously early, but it is not the characteristic tumor of infancy or the sacrococcygeal region.
incorrectas.C: Embryonal carcinoma is a primitive, highly malignant germ cell tumor typically seen in young adult testes, but it is not the specific entity associated with infant sacrococcygeal teratoma-associated presentations described here.

preguntas.q: Which malignant germ cell tumor histologically mimics the yolk sac and is also known as the endodermal sinus tumor?

e.correcta: The endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor is the most common malignant germ cell tumor in children and recapitulates yolk sac differentiation, histologically forming characteristic Schiller-Duval bodies (glomeruloid structures resembling primitive glomeruli). It secretes alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), which serves as a useful tumor marker for diagnosis and monitoring treatment response, distinguishing it from other germ cell tumors that secrete different or no markers.

incorrectas.A: Embryonal carcinoma is a highly malignant, primitive germ cell tumor composed of undifferentiated cells that can differentiate along multiple lineages, but it does not specifically mimic yolk sac architecture or produce Schiller-Duval bodies the way the endodermal sinus tumor does.
incorrectas.C: Dysgerminoma is the female counterpart of testicular seminoma, composed of uniform primitive germ cells with a 'fried egg' appearance and associated with elevated LDH, not AFP, and does not histologically resemble yolk sac tissue.
incorrectas.D: Immature teratoma contains embryonic (immature neuroectodermal) tissue from multiple germ layers and is graded by the amount of immature neural tissue present, but it does not mimic yolk sac structures — that specific histologic mimicry defines the endodermal sinus tumor alone.

preguntas.q: Which serum marker is characteristically elevated in endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor, reflecting its resemblance to fetal yolk sac tissue?

e.correcta: Endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor is the most common germ cell tumor in children and recapitulates fetal yolk sac tissue, which normally produces AFP, so tumor cells continue secreting this protein, making serum AFP a reliable marker for diagnosis and monitoring treatment response. Histologically it shows Schiller-Duval bodies (glomeruloid structures), reinforcing its yolk-sac-like differentiation.

incorrectas.A: hCG is characteristically elevated in choriocarcinoma, which recapitulates trophoblastic tissue (syncytiotrophoblasts normally secrete hCG), not yolk sac tissue, so it is not the marker tied to endodermal sinus tumor.
incorrectas.B: CA-125 is a nonspecific marker elevated in epithelial ovarian tumors (like serous cystadenocarcinoma) and various benign conditions, but it is not the characteristic marker for germ cell tumors of yolk sac lineage.
incorrectas.D: LDH is elevated in dysgerminoma (the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma) reflecting high cellular turnover, not specifically in yolk sac tumor, whose defining marker is AFP.

preguntas.q: Endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumors are characterized histologically, in about 50% of cases, by which structure?

e.correcta: Schiller-Duval bodies are glomeruloid structures — a central blood vessel surrounded by a layer of tumor cells within a space lined by more tumor cells — that morphologically mimic a primitive glomerulus, and they are found in roughly half of yolk sac tumors, making them a classic (though not universal) diagnostic clue on histology. Their presence, together with AFP positivity, supports the yolk sac tumor diagnosis.

incorrectas.A: Call-Exner bodies are small follicle-like structures containing eosinophilic material seen in granulosa cell tumors, an entirely different sex cord-stromal tumor category, not a germ cell tumor feature.
incorrectas.B: Psammoma bodies are concentric calcified structures associated with papillary lesions such as papillary serous ovarian carcinoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma, and meningioma, not yolk sac tumors.
incorrectas.D: Reinke crystals are eosinophilic cytoplasmic crystalloids found in Leydig cells (and Leydig cell tumors) of the testis, an unrelated sex cord-stromal cell type, not a feature of germ cell yolk sac tumors.

preguntas.q: A patient with choriocarcinoma develops hemoptysis and shortness of breath. This reflects which characteristic pattern of spread for this tumor?

o.A: Slow lymphatic spread to pelvic nodes only
o.B: Early, diffuse hematogenous spread, especially to the lungs
o.C: Direct local invasion without distant spread
o.D: Spread confined to the peritoneal cavity

e.correcta: Choriocarcinoma is composed of malignant cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast without chorionic villi, and it has a strong intrinsic tendency to invade blood vessels early, leading to widespread hematogenous dissemination — the lungs are the most common site, which explains hemoptysis and dyspnea, but spread to brain and liver is also common. This aggressive vascular invasion pattern (rather than slow lymphatic spread) is characteristic of trophoblastic tumors and is why choriocarcinoma can present with distant metastatic symptoms even when the primary lesion is small.

incorrectas.A: Choriocarcinoma is notorious for early hematogenous (not lymphatic) spread, so describing it as slowly spreading to pelvic nodes only misrepresents its actual aggressive vascular invasion pattern.
incorrectas.C: While local invasion of the uterus can occur, choriocarcinoma's clinically defining feature is early distant hematogenous metastasis, not confinement to local invasion, so 'without distant spread' is inconsistent with the pulmonary symptoms described.
incorrectas.D: Peritoneal spread is not the characteristic pattern for choriocarcinoma; its hallmark is hematogenous dissemination to distant organs like lung, brain, and liver, not confinement to the peritoneal cavity.

preguntas.q: Which serum marker, produced by syncytiotrophoblasts, is characteristically elevated in choriocarcinoma?

e.correcta: hCG is produced by syncytiotrophoblastic cells, which make up choriocarcinoma along with cytotrophoblasts, so this rapidly proliferating, highly vascular germ cell/gestational tumor secretes very high levels of beta-hCG. This makes hCG both a diagnostic marker and a way to monitor treatment response, since levels should fall to zero with successful therapy and rising titers signal recurrence.

incorrectas.A: AFP is a marker of yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumor and some embryonal carcinomas, reflecting a different germ cell lineage; pure choriocarcinoma does not produce AFP because it lacks yolk sac differentiation.
incorrectas.B: LDH is a nonspecific marker most classically associated with dysgerminoma (and used to track burden in that tumor), not specifically tied to the syncytiotrophoblastic secretory activity that defines choriocarcinoma.
incorrectas.D: CA-125 is a marker for epithelial ovarian tumors, particularly serous carcinomas, and is not produced by trophoblastic tissue, so it is not the characteristic marker for choriocarcinoma.

preguntas.q: Choriocarcinoma is classically associated with which type of ovarian cyst, resulting from excess hCG stimulation?

e.correcta: Choriocarcinoma secretes extremely high levels of hCG, which structurally resembles LH and can overstimulate the theca interna cells of the ovary via the LH receptor, causing bilateral theca-lutein cysts filled with luteinized theca cells. This same hCG-driven mechanism explains why theca-lutein cysts are also seen in other high-hCG states like hydatidiform mole and multiple gestation, making them a marker of excessive gonadotropin/hCG stimulation rather than a primary ovarian process.

incorrectas.A: Follicular cysts arise from a follicle that fails to rupture or involute normally during a typical menstrual cycle, a common benign finding unrelated to the massive hCG surge produced by choriocarcinoma.
incorrectas.B: A corpus luteum cyst forms from persistence of the corpus luteum after ovulation under normal physiologic hCG/LH support, not from the pathologically excessive hCG stimulation characteristic of choriocarcinoma.
incorrectas.D: A chocolate cyst (endometrioma) is a cystic collection of old hemorrhagic debris from ectopic endometrial tissue in endometriosis, a completely different pathophysiology unrelated to hCG-driven theca cell stimulation.

preguntas.q: A malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary or testis composed of large, primitive cells with an aggressive course and early metastasis is best classified as which tumor?

e.correcta: Embryonal carcinoma is a malignant germ cell tumor composed of large, primitive, anaplastic cells growing in sheets or glandular patterns, and it behaves aggressively with early hematogenous and lymphatic spread, distinguishing it from other germ cell tumors that tend to be more indolent. It is typically associated with elevated AFP and/or hCG and, unlike a mature teratoma, has no capacity for benign, well-differentiated tissue elements — its primitive, undifferentiated cell population is what drives its aggressive clinical course.

incorrectas.A: Dysgerminoma (the testicular counterpart is seminoma) is also a malignant germ cell tumor, but it is composed of uniform cells resembling primordial germ cells, is markedly radiosensitive, and generally has an excellent prognosis, unlike the aggressive, early-metastasizing behavior described here.
incorrectas.C: Mature teratoma is typically a benign tumor composed of well-differentiated tissues from all three germ layers (e.g., hair, teeth, cartilage), and it does not behave aggressively or metastasize early, contrasting sharply with embryonal carcinoma's primitive, invasive cells.
incorrectas.D: Brenner tumor is a benign (or rarely borderline) ovarian tumor of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelium, not a germ cell tumor at all, and does not display the aggressive primitive-cell morphology or early metastatic behavior described.

preguntas.q: Which is the most common malignant sex cord-stromal tumor of the ovary?

e.correcta: Granulosa cell tumor is the most common malignant sex cord-stromal tumor of the ovary, arising from the granulosa cells that normally support oocyte development and produce estrogen (and inhibin). Because these tumor cells retain estrogen-secreting capacity, patients often present with signs of estrogen excess such as precocious puberty in girls, or endometrial hyperplasia/abnormal bleeding in postmenopausal women, and Call-Exner bodies are a classic histologic clue.

incorrectas.A: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor is a sex cord-stromal tumor that classically causes virilization from androgen production, but it is far less common than granulosa cell tumor and is not the most frequent malignant entity in this category.
incorrectas.B: Fibroma is a benign sex cord-stromal tumor composed of spindle-shaped fibroblasts, notable for its association with Meigs syndrome (ascites and pleural effusion), but it is not malignant and thus does not fit the question.
incorrectas.C: Thecoma is also typically a benign, estrogen-producing sex cord-stromal tumor, distinguishing it from the malignant potential and greater frequency of granulosa cell tumor.

preguntas.q: Granulosa cell tumor of the ovary predominantly affects women in which decade of life?

e.correcta: Granulosa cell tumors are estrogen-producing sex cord-stromal tumors that most commonly present in postmenopausal women, peaking in the 50s, when unopposed estrogen production classically causes postmenopausal bleeding due to endometrial hyperplasia (and carries a risk of endometrial carcinoma). Recognizing the typical age and the estrogenic clinical picture (breast tenderness, precocious puberty in juvenile cases, or postmenopausal bleeding in adults) is key to identifying this tumor.

incorrectas.A: A juvenile variant of granulosa cell tumor can occur in children/young girls presenting with precocious puberty, but the predominant and classically tested age group for the adult form is much later in life, not the 20s.
incorrectas.B: The 30s is not the characteristic peak age; granulosa cell tumors are most typically associated with perimenopausal/postmenopausal women, well beyond this decade.
incorrectas.D: While ovarian tumors can occur in elderly women, granulosa cell tumor's classic peak is the perimenopausal/postmenopausal 50s rather than the 70s, which is more associated with epithelial tumors.

preguntas.q: A postmenopausal woman presents with abnormal uterine bleeding. Workup reveals an estrogen-secreting ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor composed of spindle cells resembling fibroblasts. What is the most likely diagnosis?

e.correcta: Thecoma is a benign sex cord-stromal tumor composed of lipid-laden, spindle-shaped theca cells that resemble fibroblasts and characteristically produce estrogen, which in a postmenopausal woman manifests as abnormal uterine bleeding from endometrial stimulation. The combination of spindle cell morphology plus estrogenic activity in an older woman is the classic clue that distinguishes thecoma from its histologic cousin, fibroma, which is hormonally silent.

incorrectas.B: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors typically secrete androgens and cause virilization/hirsutism, not estrogen-driven bleeding, so the hormonal picture described does not match this tumor.
incorrectas.C: Fibroma has essentially identical spindle-cell fibroblast-like morphology to thecoma but is classically non-functional (hormonally silent) and associated with Meigs syndrome, not estrogen secretion and bleeding.
incorrectas.D: Krukenberg tumor is a metastatic mucinous signet-ring cell adenocarcinoma (usually from stomach) to the ovary, not a hormonally active sex cord-stromal tumor, so it would not present with estrogen-mediated bleeding from spindle cells resembling fibroblasts.

preguntas.q: A rare ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor secretes androgens. Which clinical finding would this tumor most likely cause in an affected woman?

e.correcta: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors are androgen-secreting sex cord-stromal tumors, and the excess testosterone/androgen production causes virilizing features such as hirsutism, temporal balding, clitoromegaly, and voice deepening in affected women. This androgenic presentation contrasts with the estrogenic picture (bleeding, precocious puberty) seen with granulosa cell tumors and thecomas, making hormone-driven signs and symptoms a key way to distinguish among sex cord-stromal tumors.

incorrectas.A: Precocious puberty results from estrogen-secreting tumors (like juvenile granulosa cell tumor), not androgen-secreting tumors, so this does not match an androgen-producing neoplasm.
incorrectas.C: Galactorrhea is typically due to hyperprolactinemia (e.g., from a prolactinoma), unrelated to ovarian androgen secretion, so it would not be the expected finding here.
incorrectas.D: Postmenopausal bleeding results from unopposed estrogen stimulating the endometrium, as seen with thecoma or granulosa cell tumor, not from an androgen-secreting tumor, which instead causes virilization.

preguntas.q: A solid ovarian mass composed of bundles of spindle-shaped fibroblasts with white fibrous bands on gross exam, and no hormonal activity, is most consistent with which sex cord-stromal tumor?

e.correcta: Fibroma is the classic hormonally inactive (non-functioning) sex cord-stromal tumor composed of bundles of spindle-shaped fibroblasts, grossly appearing as a solid, firm mass with characteristic white, whorled fibrous bands — essentially the same cell type as thecoma but without lipid content or hormone production. It is also notable for its association with Meigs syndrome (ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion that resolves after tumor removal).

incorrectas.B: Thecoma shares similar spindle cell morphology but is lipid-laden and typically estrogen-secreting, which contradicts the 'no hormonal activity' description given for this tumor.
incorrectas.C: Granulosa cell tumor has a distinct histology (Call-Exner bodies, coffee-bean nuclei) and is characteristically estrogen-producing, not a hormonally silent spindle cell fibrous mass.
incorrectas.D: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor is composed of Sertoli and Leydig cell elements and is typically androgen-secreting, causing virilization, which does not fit the hormonally inactive fibrous tumor described.

preguntas.q: Which ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor may present with a "pulling" sensation in the groin, related to ovarian torsion or tumor traction?

e.correcta: Ovarian fibromas are benign sex cord-stromal tumors composed of spindle-shaped fibroblasts that produce dense collagen, making them solid and heavy; this weight predisposes the ovary to torsion, and both the mass effect and torsion can produce a dragging or 'pulling' sensation in the groin/pelvis. Fibromas are also classically associated with Meigs syndrome (ascites and pleural effusion resolving after tumor removal), which is a heavily tested association.

incorrectas.C: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors are androgen-secreting stromal tumors that classically cause virilization (hirsutism, clitoromegaly, voice deepening) rather than being defined by a pulling/traction sensation from a bulky, torsion-prone mass.
incorrectas.D: Granulosa cell tumors secrete estrogen and are associated with precocious puberty in girls or endometrial hyperplasia/cancer in adults, plus Call-Exner bodies histologically — their hallmark is hormonal effect, not the mechanical traction/torsion sensation seen with the dense, heavy fibroma.
incorrectas.A: Thecomas, like fibromas, are stromal tumors but are typically estrogen-secreting and present with hormonal manifestations (postmenopausal bleeding); the classic 'pulling' sensation from a heavy, torsion-prone solid mass is specifically the teaching point for fibroma.

preguntas.q: In contrast to primary mucinous ovarian tumors, which are usually unilateral, Krukenberg tumors of the ovary are typically what laterality?

e.correcta: Krukenberg tumors are metastatic signet-ring cell adenocarcinomas (classically from the stomach, but also colon or breast) that spread to the ovaries, and because metastatic spread commonly occurs via transperitoneal or hematogenous/lymphatic routes that seed both ovaries, Krukenberg tumors are characteristically bilateral. This bilaterality is a key clue that should prompt a search for an extra-ovarian (usually GI) primary rather than assuming a primary ovarian neoplasm.

incorrectas.A: Krukenberg tumors are not restricted to unilateral right-sided disease; their defining laterality pattern is bilateral involvement, reflecting metastatic rather than primary ovarian origin.
incorrectas.B: Similarly, a strictly left-sided unilateral pattern does not describe Krukenberg tumors, which are classically bilateral due to their metastatic spread pattern.
incorrectas.D: Krukenberg tumors involve the ovaries themselves (bilaterally), not a midline uterine mass; uterine involvement is not the characteristic feature being tested here.

preguntas.q: A patient with a mucinous tumor of the appendix develops massive accumulation of gelatinous mucus in the peritoneal cavity with metastasis to the ovary. What is this condition called?

e.correcta: Pseudomyxoma peritonei is the accumulation of massive amounts of mucinous, gelatinous material within the peritoneal cavity, most often arising from a mucin-producing appendiceal tumor (appendiceal mucinous neoplasm) that ruptures or seeds the peritoneum and secondarily involves the ovaries; it behaves as a slowly progressive, space-occupying process that can cause bowel obstruction over time. Recognizing the appendiceal source and gelatinous ascites is what distinguishes this entity from other causes of peritoneal spread.

incorrectas.A: Krukenberg tumor refers specifically to metastatic signet-ring cell carcinoma involving the ovaries (usually from stomach), not the diffuse gelatinous mucinous peritoneal accumulation described here.
incorrectas.B: Meigs syndrome is the triad of ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion, unrelated to mucinous appendiceal tumors or gelatinous peritoneal mucin accumulation.
incorrectas.D: Peritoneal carcinomatosis is a general term for diffuse peritoneal metastatic spread of carcinoma, but it does not specifically describe the gelatinous mucin accumulation from a mucinous appendiceal primary that defines pseudomyxoma peritonei.

preguntas.q: What is the most common specific anatomic site for an ectopic pregnancy to implant?

e.correcta: The ampulla is the widest and longest segment of the fallopian tube, where fertilization normally occurs, and it is also the most common site for a fertilized egg to implant ectopically when normal transport to the uterus is delayed or obstructed — accounting for the majority of tubal ectopic pregnancies. Because the tube lacks the distensibility and vascular support of the uterine wall, implantation here poses a high risk of rupture as the pregnancy grows.

incorrectas.B: Ovarian ectopic pregnancy does occur but is rare compared to tubal implantation; the ampulla of the fallopian tube is by far the most common site overall.
incorrectas.C: Cervical ectopic pregnancy is an uncommon and distinct entity, not the most common site; tubal (ampullary) implantation vastly outnumbers cervical implantation.
incorrectas.D: Abdominal ectopic pregnancy is rare and usually results from secondary implantation after tubal abortion, not the primary and most common site of ectopic implantation.

preguntas.q: A woman presents with right lower quadrant pain and a positive pregnancy test. This presentation of ectopic pregnancy is often clinically mistaken for which condition?

e.correcta: Ectopic pregnancy, especially when it implants in the right fallopian tube, classically presents with right lower quadrant pain, and combined with nausea and a low-grade inflammatory response, this can closely mimic appendicitis on initial clinical assessment. This is why a pregnancy test (beta-hCG) is a critical, easily overlooked step in any woman of reproductive age presenting with RLQ pain, to avoid misdiagnosing a ruptured ectopic as appendicitis.

incorrectas.A: Cholecystitis presents with right upper quadrant pain, often after fatty meals, with different associated findings (Murphy sign), and is not the classic mimicker of RLQ ectopic pregnancy pain.
incorrectas.C: Diverticulitis classically causes left lower quadrant pain (given the predominance of sigmoid diverticula), which is the opposite side from the classic right-sided mimicry of appendicitis by ectopic pregnancy.
incorrectas.D: Pyelonephritis typically presents with flank pain, fever, and costovertebral angle tenderness rather than the RLQ pain pattern that leads to confusion with appendicitis.

preguntas.q: What is the key risk factor for ectopic pregnancy?

e.correcta: Tubal scarring — most often from prior pelvic inflammatory disease (e.g., chlamydia or gonorrhea salpingitis), previous tubal surgery, or endometriosis — impairs the normal ciliary and peristaltic transport of the fertilized egg through the fallopian tube, causing it to implant within the tube itself rather than reaching the uterus. This mechanical/functional obstruction is the dominant risk factor for ectopic pregnancy and is why a history of PID or tubal surgery is such an important part of the history in a patient with suspected ectopic pregnancy.

incorrectas.A: Uterine fibroids can affect fertility and implantation within the uterus but are not the classic risk factor for ectopic (tubal) implantation, which relates to impaired tubal transport rather than uterine cavity distortion.
incorrectas.C: Bicornuate uterus is a congenital uterine anomaly associated with pregnancy complications like preterm labor and malpresentation, not specifically the major risk factor for ectopic pregnancy.
incorrectas.D: Multiple gestation (e.g., from fertility treatment) can be associated with ectopic pregnancy in some contexts, but it is not the key, most classically tested risk factor — tubal scarring from infection or surgery is.

preguntas.q: A woman presents with amenorrhea followed weeks later by abdominal pain. Which location of pain is classic for ectopic pregnancy?

e.correcta: In ectopic pregnancy, the growing gestational mass within the fallopian tube produces localized peritoneal irritation and stretching of the tube on the affected side, so pain is classically unilateral, in the lower quadrant corresponding to the involved tube. This localized lower quadrant pain, together with amenorrhea and a positive pregnancy test, forms the classic triad that should prompt urgent evaluation for ectopic pregnancy, especially before rupture and hemoperitoneum occur.

incorrectas.A: Epigastric pain is not the characteristic location for ectopic pregnancy; it would be unusual and more suggestive of an upper GI or pancreaticobiliary process.
incorrectas.C: Pain confined strictly to the suprapubic midline is more typical of a uterine process (like threatened abortion) rather than the unilateral lower quadrant pain from a tubal ectopic mass.
incorrectas.D: Bilateral flank pain suggests a renal or upper urinary tract process (e.g., pyelonephritis) rather than the unilateral lower quadrant pain classically produced by tubal ectopic pregnancy.

preguntas.q: Which of the following are major complications of ectopic pregnancy that make it a surgical emergency?

e.correcta: As an ectopic pregnancy grows within the narrow, non-distensible fallopian tube, it can cause blood to collect within the tube (hematosalpinx) and ultimately cause the tube to rupture, leading to acute intraperitoneal hemorrhage — a life-threatening surgical emergency requiring immediate intervention. This mechanical inability of the tube to accommodate a growing pregnancy, unlike the uterus, is the fundamental reason ectopic pregnancy is dangerous and time-sensitive.

incorrectas.A: Placenta accreta and abruption are complications of an intrauterine pregnancy with abnormal placental attachment or separation, not complications of a tubal ectopic pregnancy.
incorrectas.C: Preeclampsia and eclampsia are hypertensive disorders of pregnancy that develop in the context of an ongoing intrauterine pregnancy with placental involvement, not a feature of ectopic (extrauterine) implantation.
incorrectas.D: Spontaneous abortion and stillbirth refer to loss of an intrauterine pregnancy, not the structural rupture/hemorrhage complications specific to a tubal ectopic pregnancy.

preguntas.q: Spontaneous abortion is defined as miscarriage of a fetus before which gestational age?

e.correcta: Spontaneous abortion (miscarriage) is defined as pregnancy loss before 20 weeks gestation, the threshold conventionally used to distinguish it from stillbirth (fetal death at or after 20 weeks), largely because 20 weeks approximates the boundary of potential fetal viability used in obstetric classification. Most spontaneous abortions occur in the first trimester and are commonly due to chromosomal abnormalities, making this an important epidemiologic and clinical cutoff.

incorrectas.A: 12 weeks marks the end of the first trimester, a clinically relevant milestone for screening and risk stratification, but it is not the gestational age cutoff that defines spontaneous abortion.
incorrectas.B: 16 weeks falls within the second trimester and does not correspond to any standard obstetric definition boundary for spontaneous abortion versus stillbirth.
incorrectas.D: 24 weeks is sometimes cited as a threshold related to extrauterine viability in neonatal care discussions, but it is not the gestational age used to define spontaneous abortion, which is set at 20 weeks.

preguntas.q: Approximately what fraction of recognizable pregnancies end in spontaneous abortion?

e.correcta: Approximately 1 in 4 (25%) of recognized/clinically apparent pregnancies end in spontaneous abortion, most commonly in the first trimester and most often due to chromosomal abnormalities in the conceptus (such as aneuploidy). This figure is higher when counting all conceptions, since many pregnancies are lost before they are ever clinically recognized, but among recognized pregnancies the roughly 25% rate is the classically cited statistic.

incorrectas.A: 1/10 underestimates the true rate of spontaneous abortion among recognized pregnancies — the classically taught figure is closer to 1 in 4, reflecting how common early pregnancy loss actually is.
incorrectas.C: 1/2 overstates the loss rate for clinically recognized pregnancies; a rate that high is closer to estimates of total pregnancy loss including very early, unrecognized losses before a clinical pregnancy is even confirmed.
incorrectas.D: 3/4 would imply that spontaneous abortion is the most common outcome of recognized pregnancy, which is far higher than the accepted approximately 25% figure and does not reflect reality for confirmed pregnancies.

preguntas.q: A pregnant woman presents with vaginal bleeding, cramp-like pelvic pain, and passage of fetal tissue. What is the most likely diagnosis?

e.correcta: Spontaneous abortion presents with vaginal bleeding, cramping pelvic pain from uterine contractions expelling the products of conception, and passage of recognizable fetal or placental tissue — this triad directly reflects the uterus actively expelling an intrauterine pregnancy that has failed, most often due to a chromosomal abnormality. The presence of passed tissue is the key differentiator from other causes of first-trimester bleeding that do not involve expulsion of conceptus.

incorrectas.A: Placenta previa causes painless vaginal bleeding in the third trimester due to abnormal placental position over the cervical os, not cramping with passage of fetal tissue in an ongoing pregnancy loss.
incorrectas.B: Ectopic pregnancy causes unilateral lower quadrant pain and bleeding from an extrauterine implantation, but it does not involve passage of fetal tissue vaginally since the pregnancy is not developing within the uterine cavity to be expelled that way.
incorrectas.D: Placental abruption presents with painful vaginal bleeding due to premature placental separation, typically later in pregnancy, and is not characterized by passage of fetal tissue as seen in a completed or ongoing miscarriage.

preguntas.q: Spontaneous abortion is most often caused by which type of anomaly, especially trisomy 16?

e.correcta: The majority of spontaneous abortions, particularly those occurring in the first trimester, result from chromosomal abnormalities (commonly autosomal trisomies, with trisomy 16 being the single most common trisomy found in miscarriage tissue) that are incompatible with normal development. These genetic errors typically arise from meiotic nondisjunction during gametogenesis, and their frequency explains why chromosomal analysis of products of conception is often pursued after recurrent pregnancy loss.

incorrectas.B: Infections (e.g., TORCH organisms, Listeria) can cause pregnancy loss but account for a much smaller proportion of spontaneous abortions compared to chromosomal causes, and are not specifically linked to trisomy 16.
incorrectas.C: Anatomic uterine anomalies (like septate uterus) are a recognized but less common cause of pregnancy loss, more often implicated in recurrent second-trimester loss rather than being the dominant overall cause tied to trisomy 16.
incorrectas.D: Autoimmune causes such as antiphospholipid syndrome contribute to recurrent pregnancy loss but are not the most common overall cause of spontaneous abortion, and are unrelated to trisomy 16.

preguntas.q: Exposure to a teratogen during the first two weeks of gestation (the "all-or-none" period) most commonly results in which outcome?

e.correcta: During the first two weeks of gestation (before implantation is complete and organogenesis has begun), embryonic cells are still largely totipotent/pluripotent, so a teratogenic insult either damages so few critical cells that the embryo fully recovers with no lasting effect, or it damages enough cells that the embryo does not survive — hence the term 'all-or-none.' This is why teratogen exposure in this very early window classically manifests as spontaneous abortion (or no effect at all) rather than a specific structural birth defect.

incorrectas.A: Organ hypoplasia is more characteristic of teratogen exposure later in gestation (the fetal period), when organs are already formed and undergoing growth, not during the pre-organogenesis all-or-none period.
incorrectas.B: Organ malformation is the hallmark of teratogen exposure during the embryonic period of organogenesis (weeks 3-8), when organ primordia are actively forming, not during the first two weeks before organogenesis begins.
incorrectas.D: Functional or behavioral defects are associated with teratogen exposure during the fetal period (after organogenesis is complete), when organs are maturing functionally, not the earliest all-or-none window.

preguntas.q: Teratogen exposure during weeks 3-8 of gestation (the period of organogenesis) most commonly results in which outcome?

o.D: No effect due to placental barrier

e.correcta: Weeks 3-8 constitute the embryonic period of organogenesis, when the primordia of essentially all major organ systems are actively forming from the germ layers; a teratogenic insult during this critical window disrupts the specific developmental program of whichever organ is forming at that time, producing structural malformations (e.g., neural tube defects, cardiac septal defects, limb anomalies) rather than simple loss of the pregnancy or reduced organ size. This is why organogenesis is considered the period of greatest teratogenic vulnerability for birth defects.

incorrectas.A: Spontaneous abortion is the classic outcome of teratogen exposure during the pre-implantation/pre-organogenesis all-or-none period (first two weeks), not during active organogenesis when organs are forming and malformed rather than lost.
incorrectas.C: Organ hypoplasia (reduced organ size/growth) is more typical of teratogen exposure during the later fetal period, once organs are already formed and are instead growing/maturing, not during the formative organogenesis window.
incorrectas.D: No effect due to placental barrier is incorrect reasoning — the placenta is not a reliable barrier against many teratogens, and organogenesis is in fact the period of highest susceptibility to structural malformation.

preguntas.q: Teratogen exposure occurring after week 8 of gestation (the fetal period) most commonly results in which effect?

e.correcta: After week 8, the fetal period begins, during which major organ structures have already formed and the fetus is primarily undergoing growth, maturation, and functional development; teratogen exposure at this stage more often stunts the growth of already-formed organs (hypoplasia) or causes subtler functional/behavioral deficits rather than the gross structural malformations typical of the earlier organogenesis window. This time-dependent shift in teratogen effect (all-or-none to malformation to hypoplasia/functional deficit) is a classic embryology teaching point.

incorrectas.A: Spontaneous abortion is the characteristic outcome of the very earliest pre-organogenesis period (first two weeks), not the fetal period after week 8, when the pregnancy is already well-established structurally.
incorrectas.B: Organ malformation is the hallmark of teratogen exposure during organogenesis (weeks 3-8), when organ primordia are still forming; by the fetal period, organs are already formed, so growth disturbance (hypoplasia) is more typical than new malformation.
incorrectas.D: Neural tube defects arise from disruption of neural tube closure, which occurs by around week 4 (within the embryonic period), not from teratogen exposure after week 8 when neural tube closure has long since occurred.

preguntas.q: Which of the following is a recognized risk factor for placenta previa?

e.correcta: Prior cesarean section leaves a scar on the lower uterine segment, which alters normal endometrial architecture and vascularity, predisposing the placenta in a subsequent pregnancy to implant abnormally low in the uterus (previa) or over the scarred area — this same scarring also underlies the associated risk of placenta accreta spectrum disorders. This link between prior uterine surgery and abnormal placental implantation is a recurring theme connecting previa and accreta on exams.

incorrectas.A: Nulliparity is not a classic risk factor for placenta previa; in fact, previa risk increases with increasing parity and prior uterine surgery, the opposite of a nulliparity association.
incorrectas.C: Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder related to abnormal placental vascular development and maternal endothelial dysfunction, but it is not a recognized risk factor for the abnormal low placental implantation seen in previa.
incorrectas.D: Post-term pregnancy relates to prolonged gestation beyond 42 weeks and its own set of complications (e.g., macrosomia, oligohydramnios), but it is not associated with the abnormal placental positioning seen in placenta previa.

preguntas.q: Premature separation of the placenta from the uterine wall (decidua) prior to delivery of the fetus is known as placental what?

e.correcta: Placental abruption is the premature separation of a normally implanted placenta from the decidua before delivery, typically due to rupture of maternal decidual vessels causing retroplacental hemorrhage; this separation compromises fetal oxygenation and nutrient supply and classically presents with painful vaginal bleeding, uterine tenderness, and fetal distress. Risk factors include hypertension, trauma, cocaine use, and prior abruption, and it is a major cause of third-trimester bleeding along with previa.

incorrectas.A: Previa refers to abnormal placental position overlying or near the internal cervical os, not premature separation of a normally positioned placenta, and previa classically causes painless (not painful) bleeding.
incorrectas.C: Accreta refers to abnormal firm attachment of the placenta to the myometrium without a cleavage plane at delivery, a distinct problem of attachment depth rather than premature separation before delivery.
incorrectas.D: Percreta refers to placental invasion completely through the myometrium and into or beyond the uterine serosa (sometimes into adjacent organs), which is again an attachment/invasion disorder, not premature separation of the placenta.

preguntas.q: Placental abruption can compromise fetal oxygenation and blood supply, potentially leading to which severe fetal outcome?

e.correcta: Placental abruption causes premature separation of the placenta from the uterine wall, disrupting the maternal-fetal blood and oxygen exchange interface; if severe or prolonged enough, this can progress to fetal hypoxia and death in utero, i.e., stillbirth. This is why abruption is managed as an obstetric emergency, with prompt delivery often required to prevent fetal demise once significant separation is suspected.

incorrectas.A: Macrosomia (large-for-gestational-age fetus) results from conditions like maternal diabetes with fetal hyperinsulinemia, not from disrupted placental blood supply, which instead threatens fetal growth and oxygenation rather than promoting excess growth.
incorrectas.C: Polyhydramnios (excess amniotic fluid) is associated with conditions like fetal anomalies impairing swallowing or maternal diabetes, not with placental abruption, which compromises perfusion rather than altering amniotic fluid dynamics.
incorrectas.D: Post-term gestation refers to a pregnancy extending beyond 42 weeks and has no direct relationship to placental abruption, which is an acute vascular event that threatens the fetus during the pregnancy rather than affecting its duration.

preguntas.q: Which placenta accreta spectrum disorder is defined by abnormal attachment of the placenta directly to the myometrium without penetrating it?

e.correcta: Placenta accreta is defined by abnormal attachment of chorionic villi directly to the myometrium (due to a defective or absent decidua basalis), without the placenta actually invading into the muscle itself; this is the mildest form of the placenta accreta spectrum but still prevents normal separation at delivery and can cause severe postpartum hemorrhage. It is distinguished from increta (invades into the myometrium) and percreta (invades through and beyond the myometrium) purely by depth of penetration.

incorrectas.A: Previa describes the placenta's position relative to the cervical os (covering or near it), an entirely separate concept from the depth of myometrial attachment/invasion that defines the accreta spectrum.
incorrectas.B: Increta specifically means the placental villi invade into the myometrium (beyond simple attachment), which is a deeper, more severe degree of invasion than the attachment-only definition of accreta.
incorrectas.D: Percreta describes invasion completely through the myometrium and often into the uterine serosa or adjacent structures, representing the most severe end of the spectrum, well beyond the attachment-only picture of accreta.

preguntas.q: Which term describes abnormal penetration of the placenta into (but not through) the myometrium?

e.correcta: Increta is the placenta accreta spectrum disorder in which chorionic villi actually invade into the substance of the myometrium (rather than merely attaching to its surface as in accreta), reflecting a deeper defect in the decidua basalis that fails to properly limit trophoblastic invasion. This intermediate degree of invasion increases the risk of massive hemorrhage at delivery and often necessitates hysterectomy, distinguishing it from the more superficial accreta and the more extensive percreta.

incorrectas.A: Accreta refers to placental attachment directly to the myometrial surface without penetrating into the muscle itself, which is a shallower degree of abnormal attachment than the invasion into the myometrium described here.
incorrectas.C: Percreta describes invasion completely through the full thickness of the myometrium and beyond (into the serosa or adjacent organs), which is deeper than invasion into (but not through) the myometrium.
incorrectas.D: Previa refers to the placenta's location relative to the internal cervical os, a positional abnormality unrelated to the depth of myometrial invasion being described.

preguntas.q: Which placenta accreta spectrum disorder involves penetration of the placenta through the myometrium and into the uterine serosa, sometimes attaching to the bladder or rectum?

e.correcta: Placenta percreta is the most severe form of the placenta accreta spectrum, in which chorionic villi invade completely through the myometrium and breach the uterine serosa, sometimes extending into adjacent pelvic organs like the bladder or rectum. All accreta spectrum disorders arise from a defective decidua basalis (often from prior cesarean scarring or prior curettage), which normally acts as a cleavage plane limiting trophoblastic invasion; when it is deficient, villi attach directly to or invade through myometrium with no natural boundary. The depth of invasion (accreta < increta < percreta) determines both surgical risk and the likelihood of needing hysterectomy.

incorrectas.A: Accreta is the mildest form, where villi attach directly to the myometrium without invading it and without penetrating into or through the muscle layer, so it does not reach the serosa or adjacent organs.
incorrectas.B: Increta involves villi invading into the myometrium itself, but stopping short of breaching the serosal surface — it lacks the full-thickness penetration and organ involvement that defines percreta.
incorrectas.D: Placental abruption is a completely distinct entity: premature separation of a normally implanted placenta from the uterine wall causing hemorrhage, not an abnormality of placental attachment depth, so it does not fit a question about myometrial/serosal invasion.

preguntas.q: Placenta accreta spectrum disorders classically present after delivery with failure of placental separation and which additional finding?

o.A: Painless bleeding in the third trimester

e.correcta: Because the placenta in accreta spectrum disorders is abnormally adherent (or invasive) into the myometrium, it fails to separate cleanly from the uterine wall after delivery of the fetus, and manual attempts at removal tear through richly vascularized myometrial tissue rather than through the normal decidual cleavage plane. This produces massive, often life-threatening postpartum hemorrhage, since the uterus cannot contract down effectively on the retained/adherent placental tissue to achieve hemostasis. This combination of retained placenta plus severe post-partum bleeding is the classic clinical presentation that should trigger suspicion for an accreta spectrum disorder.

incorrectas.A: Painless bright red bleeding in the third trimester is the classic presentation of placenta previa, not accreta spectrum disorders, which typically present at the time of attempted delivery rather than antenatally.
incorrectas.C: Elevated blood pressure with proteinuria describes preeclampsia, an entirely separate hypertensive disorder of pregnancy unrelated to abnormal placental attachment depth.
incorrectas.D: Recurrent early pregnancy loss points toward causes like antiphospholipid syndrome, chromosomal abnormalities, or uterine anomalies — it is not a feature of accreta spectrum disorders, which manifest at delivery, not as early losses.

preguntas.q: Placenta accreta, due to abnormal attachment of the placenta to the uterus, often requires which definitive procedure after delivery?

e.correcta: Because the placenta in accreta is abnormally adherent to or invading the myometrium, it often cannot be safely or completely separated from the uterus, and forceful attempts at manual removal risk uncontrollable hemorrhage and uterine rupture. Hysterectomy removes the entire uterus along with the retained/invasive placental tissue, providing definitive hemostasis when the placenta cannot be extracted piecemeal, and is frequently planned in advance when accreta is diagnosed antenatally by ultrasound/MRI. This is why cesarean hysterectomy is considered the standard definitive management, especially for the more invasive increta/percreta forms.

incorrectas.A: Uterine curettage is used to remove retained tissue after an incomplete abortion or for molar pregnancy evacuation, but scraping an accreta placenta risks perforating the myometrium and causing catastrophic bleeding rather than achieving control.
incorrectas.C: Cervical cerclage is a preventive suture placed to reinforce an incompetent cervix earlier in pregnancy to prevent preterm birth; it has no role in managing an already-delivered, abnormally adherent placenta.
incorrectas.D: Tubal ligation is an elective sterilization procedure on the fallopian tubes and does nothing to address a placenta that is invading the myometrium or the hemorrhage risk it poses.

preguntas.q: A pregnant woman at 24 weeks gestation has a blood pressure of 150/95 mmHg with no proteinuria, no pre-existing hypertension, and no end-organ damage. What is the most likely diagnosis?

e.correcta: Gestational hypertension is defined as new-onset blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg after 20 weeks gestation in a woman without prior hypertension, and critically, without proteinuria or other signs of end-organ damage — exactly the picture described here. It reflects an exaggerated maternal vascular response to pregnancy that has not yet (or will not) progress to the multisystem endothelial damage seen in preeclampsia, though patients need continued monitoring because some do progress. Distinguishing it from preeclampsia matters clinically because preeclampsia carries risks of seizure, HELLP, and placental insufficiency that change management.

incorrectas.B: Preeclampsia requires hypertension after 20 weeks PLUS proteinuria or other evidence of end-organ dysfunction (elevated creatinine, low platelets, elevated liver enzymes, pulmonary edema, or new headache/visual symptoms) — the explicit absence of proteinuria and end-organ damage here rules it out.
incorrectas.A: Chronic hypertension is diagnosed when elevated blood pressure predates pregnancy or is identified before 20 weeks gestation, but this patient is at 24 weeks with no mention of pre-existing hypertension, so a new diagnosis at 24 weeks without prior history fits gestational hypertension instead.
incorrectas.D: Eclampsia refers to new-onset tonic-clonic seizures in a woman with preeclampsia; there is no seizure activity described here, and the case doesn't even meet criteria for preeclampsia itself given the absent proteinuria/end-organ damage.

preguntas.q: Preeclampsia typically presents in relation to which gestational milestone, such that presentation before this point should raise suspicion for molar pregnancy instead?

o.C: Only in the third trimester after 36 weeks

e.correcta: Preeclampsia is defined by the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists as new hypertension with proteinuria (or other end-organ dysfunction) occurring after 20 weeks of gestation, reflecting the time needed for abnormal placentation and the resulting antiangiogenic/inflammatory cascade to produce systemic endothelial injury. Presentation of preeclampsia-like hypertension before 20 weeks is atypical and should prompt evaluation for molar pregnancy, since the markedly hyperproliferative, hypervascular trophoblastic tissue in a mole can trigger the same hypertensive/proteinuric syndrome much earlier than a normal pregnancy would. Recognizing this exception is a classic board point linking gestational trophoblastic disease to early preeclampsia-like presentations.

incorrectas.A: Before the 12th week is far too early even for the exceptional cases caused by molar pregnancy to be the expected preeclampsia cutoff; it is the reason to suspect a mole precisely because it is inconsistent with ordinary preeclampsia timing.
incorrectas.C: Restricting preeclampsia only to the third trimester after 36 weeks is too narrow, as it can develop any time from 20 weeks gestation through the postpartum period.
incorrectas.D: Preeclampsia is not restricted to onset during labor; it is a systemic disorder that develops over the antepartum course after 20 weeks and can also first appear or persist postpartum, not exclusively at delivery.

preguntas.q: Preeclampsia is caused by abnormal development of which placental structures, leading to endothelial dysfunction, vasoconstriction, and ischemia?

e.correcta: Preeclampsia results from abnormal remodeling of the spiral arteries, the maternal vessels that normally undergo trophoblastic invasion and convert from narrow, muscular vessels into wide, low-resistance conduits that supply blood to the placental intervillous space. When this invasion is incomplete, the spiral arteries remain narrow and high-resistance, causing placental hypoperfusion and ischemia, which triggers release of antiangiogenic factors (like sFlt-1) into the maternal circulation that cause widespread endothelial dysfunction, vasoconstriction, and the hypertension/proteinuria seen clinically. This spiral artery remodeling defect is the central pathophysiologic mechanism tested repeatedly for preeclampsia.

incorrectas.B: Umbilical veins carry oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus and are not the site of the trophoblastic invasion defect that initiates preeclampsia's pathophysiology.
incorrectas.C: Chorionic villi capillaries are fetal-side vessels within the villi that exchange gases and nutrients with maternal blood, but the primary lesion in preeclampsia is on the maternal spiral artery side, not villous capillary development.
incorrectas.D: Uterine venous sinuses are not the structures implicated in preeclampsia pathogenesis; the disease centers on failed conversion of maternal spiral arteries into low-resistance vessels, not venous drainage.

preguntas.q: Increased incidence of preeclampsia is seen in patients with pre-existing diabetes, chronic renal disease, autoimmune disorders, and which other pre-existing condition?

e.correcta: Chronic (pre-existing) hypertension is a well-established risk factor for preeclampsia because baseline vascular and endothelial dysfunction compounds the abnormal placentation and antiangiogenic state that drives preeclampsia, making superimposed preeclampsia much more likely in these patients. Along with pregestational diabetes, chronic renal disease, and autoimmune conditions like antiphospholipid syndrome or lupus — all of which independently damage vascular endothelium or promote a prothrombotic/inflammatory state — pre-existing hypertension rounds out the classic list of risk factors that impair normal spiral artery remodeling. Recognizing these risk factors matters clinically for risk-stratifying and initiating prophylactic low-dose aspirin in pregnancy.

incorrectas.B: Asthma is a chronic airway inflammatory disease without a recognized mechanistic link to abnormal placentation or endothelial dysfunction, so it is not among the classic preeclampsia risk factors.
incorrectas.C: Hypothyroidism, when adequately treated, is not a major established risk factor for preeclampsia in the way that hypertension, diabetes, renal disease, and autoimmune disease are.
incorrectas.D: Osteoporosis is a disorder of bone mineral density with no plausible connection to placental vascular development or endothelial injury, so it does not raise preeclampsia risk.

preguntas.q: HELLP syndrome can lead to severe hypotension due to rupture of which hepatic complication?

e.correcta: HELLP syndrome (Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets) is a severe variant of preeclampsia in which hepatic ischemia and periportal necrosis from microvascular injury can lead to intrahepatic or subcapsular hematoma formation; if this hematoma ruptures through Glisson's capsule, it causes sudden massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage and profound hypotension/hypovolemic shock. This is a life-threatening surgical emergency that requires immediate recognition (often heralded by right upper quadrant or epigastric pain) since hepatic rupture carries high maternal mortality if not treated emergently. Awareness of subcapsular hematoma as the substrate for rupture is why abdominal pain in a HELLP patient is taken so seriously.

incorrectas.B: Hepatic abscess is an infectious/suppurative process unrelated to the microvascular, ischemic liver injury of HELLP syndrome, and is not the mechanism behind sudden hypotension in these patients.
