incorrectas.B: Burkitt lymphoma is composed of intermediate-sized cells with a high proliferative rate producing a 'starry sky' pattern (macrophages engulfing apoptotic debris), growing diffusely rather than forming follicle-like nodules.
incorrectas.D: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma effaces nodal architecture with sheets of large B cells in a diffuse pattern, not organized follicles, and can in fact arise from transformation of FL rather than being defined by nodular follicle formation itself.

preguntas.q: Follicular lymphoma most commonly presents in which age group?

e.correcta: FL is an indolent lymphoma typically diagnosed in older adults, with a median age in the 60s, consistent with the time it takes to accumulate the initiating t(14;18) translocation plus the additional genetic hits needed for overt lymphoma. Its slow growth also means it is often discovered incidentally as painless lymphadenopathy later in life rather than presenting acutely.

incorrectas.A: Pediatric lymphomas are typically aggressive types such as Burkitt or lymphoblastic lymphoma; classic indolent FL as described here is rare in childhood.
incorrectas.B: Adolescence is not the typical age of presentation for an indolent, slow-accumulating neoplasm like FL; aggressive NHL subtypes are more characteristic of this younger age group.
incorrectas.C: Young adulthood is instead the first peak of Hodgkin lymphoma's bimodal age distribution, whereas FL incidence rises steadily with age rather than peaking in the 20s.

preguntas.q: The BCL2 gene, overexpressed in follicular lymphoma, is located on which chromosome?

e.correcta: BCL2 resides on chromosome 18. In follicular lymphoma, the t(14;18) translocation moves BCL2 next to the strong immunoglobulin heavy chain enhancer on chromosome 14, driving BCL2 overexpression. Because BCL2 is an antiapoptotic protein, this blocks the normal death of centrocytes that fail germinal center selection, allowing abnormal clonal survival and expansion.

incorrectas.B: Chromosome 14 houses the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus — the translocation partner site whose strong enhancer drives BCL2 overexpression — not the location of BCL2 itself.
incorrectas.C: Chromosome 8 is the location of MYC, the oncogene translocated in Burkitt lymphoma via t(8;14), a different gene and disease entity from BCL2/follicular lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: Chromosome 9 carries ABL1, involved in the Philadelphia chromosome translocation t(9;22) in CML, unrelated to BCL2 or follicular lymphoma.

preguntas.q: The immunoglobulin heavy chain gene locus, frequently hijacked by oncogene translocations in B-cell lymphomas, is located on which chromosome?

e.correcta: The IgH locus is on chromosome 14 and is highly, constitutively transcribed in B cells as part of normal antibody production. Translocations that place an oncogene next to this locus — BCL2 in follicular lymphoma via t(14;18), or MYC in Burkitt lymphoma via t(8;14) — hijack that strong enhancer activity, driving marked overexpression of what should be a tightly regulated gene.

incorrectas.A: Chromosome 18 is the location of BCL2, the translocation partner gene in follicular lymphoma, not the IgH locus itself.
incorrectas.C: Chromosome 8 is the location of MYC, the translocation partner in Burkitt lymphoma, not the IgH locus.
incorrectas.D: Chromosome 22 contains BCR, the partner gene fused with ABL1 (on chromosome 9) in the CML Philadelphia chromosome translocation, unrelated to the IgH locus.

preguntas.q: Why does translocating an oncogene (such as BCL2) next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus lead to that oncogene's overexpression?

o.A: The IgH locus is normally silenced, and translocation removes its repression
o.B: The IgH locus undergoes site-specific DNA amplification
o.C: The IgH locus is constitutively and highly transcriptionally active in B cells
o.D: The IgH locus contains a tumor suppressor that is inactivated by the translocation

e.correcta: B cells continuously and robustly transcribe immunoglobulin heavy chain genes as part of normal antibody production. When an oncogene is relocated next to the IgH locus's powerful regulatory elements, it comes under the influence of that same ongoing, high-level transcription, causing marked overexpression of a gene (like BCL2 in follicular lymphoma or MYC in Burkitt lymphoma) that would otherwise be tightly regulated.

incorrectas.A: This describes the opposite of the actual mechanism — the IgH locus is not silenced but actively and strongly transcribed, and it is this ongoing activity that gets hijacked, not a release from repression.
incorrectas.B: The mechanism is transcriptional dysregulation via juxtaposition to a strong enhancer, not an increase in gene copy number through DNA amplification.
incorrectas.D: IgH is not a tumor suppressor gene; the translocation works by placing an oncogene like BCL2 under IgH's strong regulatory control, activating rather than inactivating a growth-controlling gene.

preguntas.q: In symptomatic follicular lymphoma requiring treatment, low-dose chemotherapy is often combined with which targeted monoclonal antibody?

e.correcta: Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody directed against CD20, a surface marker expressed on the neoplastic B cells of follicular lymphoma (and most B-cell NHLs). Binding CD20 triggers complement- and antibody-dependent cytotoxicity that depletes malignant B cells, and it is typically added to chemotherapy only once a patient becomes symptomatic, since FL is indolent and asymptomatic disease is often managed with watchful waiting.

incorrectas.A: Trastuzumab targets HER2/neu and is used in HER2-positive breast cancer, a completely different target and disease from CD20-positive B-cell lymphoma.
incorrectas.B: Bevacizumab is an anti-VEGF antibody used for antiangiogenic therapy in solid tumors like colorectal and renal cell carcinoma, not a B-cell-targeted therapy for lymphoma.
incorrectas.C: Cetuximab is an anti-EGFR antibody used in colorectal and head and neck cancers with wild-type KRAS, unrelated to CD20-expressing lymphomas like FL.

preguntas.q: Follicular lymphoma may transform into which more aggressive lymphoma, presenting as a rapidly enlarging lymph node?

e.correcta: FL can acquire additional genetic alterations (such as MYC or TP53 changes) over time and transform into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, a clinically aggressive large B-cell process. This transformation should be suspected when a patient with known indolent FL develops a rapidly enlarging mass, rising LDH, or new B symptoms, and it shifts management toward aggressive chemotherapy regimens.

incorrectas.B: Burkitt lymphoma is a distinct, highly aggressive NHL driven primarily by a MYC translocation (t(8;14)), typically arising de novo or in association with EBV/immunodeficiency, rather than being the classic transformation product of FL.
incorrectas.C: Mantle cell lymphoma arises from naive mantle zone B cells with cyclin D1 overexpression from t(11;14) — a separate lymphoma entity from the start, not a transformation outcome of FL.
incorrectas.D: Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by Reed-Sternberg cells in a distinctive reactive background, a categorically different disease from NHL, and is not the typical transformation pathway for FL.

preguntas.q: Follicular lymphoma is distinguished histologically from reactive follicular hyperplasia primarily by which finding?

o.B: Disruption/effacement of normal lymph node architecture by neoplastic follicles
o.C: A preserved sinusoidal pattern with polyclonal follicles

e.correcta: In FL, back-to-back neoplastic follicles efface and replace the normal nodal architecture — including blurring the cortex-medulla distinction and invading the capsule — because this is a true monoclonal neoplastic process rather than a physiologic immune response. Reactive hyperplasia, by contrast, keeps follicles confined to the cortex with preserved overall nodal zonation.

incorrectas.A: Tingible body macrophages are actually characteristically absent within FL follicles (because BCL2 overexpression blocks the apoptosis that normally requires their clean-up function) and present in reactive hyperplasia — so this finding points toward hyperplasia, not toward FL.
incorrectas.C: A preserved sinusoidal pattern with polyclonal follicles describes reactive hyperplasia, the opposite of FL, which is defined by architectural effacement and a monoclonal, not polyclonal, B-cell population.
incorrectas.D: A well-demarcated cortex-medulla junction is also a feature of preserved reactive architecture, not FL, where the neoplastic process blurs and destroys normal nodal zonation.

preguntas.q: Follicular lymphoma follicles characteristically lack which cell type, one that is normally abundant in the germinal centers of reactive follicular hyperplasia?

e.correcta: Tingible body macrophages normally engulf apoptotic B cells that fail germinal center selection, a process that requires active apoptosis. In FL, BCL2 overexpression from t(14;18) blocks this apoptosis, so cells that should die instead survive, leaving the follicle relatively 'clean' and macrophage-poor — a useful low-power histologic clue distinguishing neoplastic from reactive follicles.

incorrectas.A: Follicular dendritic cells form the meshwork scaffold in both reactive and neoplastic follicles; their presence does not distinguish FL from hyperplasia.
incorrectas.B: Centrocytes (small cleaved B cells) are present in both reactive germinal centers and FL follicles — it is their abnormal survival and monoclonality in FL that differs, not the cell type's presence itself.
incorrectas.D: Plasma cells are typically found in the medullary cords rather than germinal centers, and their presence or absence is not the classic differentiating feature between FL and reactive hyperplasia.

preguntas.q: Immunohistochemical expression of which protein within germinal center follicles helps distinguish follicular lymphoma from reactive follicular hyperplasia?

e.correcta: Normal germinal center B cells downregulate BCL2 to allow apoptosis during the rigorous selection of high-affinity antibody-producing clones, so reactive germinal centers are BCL2-negative. In FL, the t(14;18) translocation causes BCL2 to be aberrantly overexpressed within neoplastic follicles, making BCL2 positivity a key diagnostic clue that favors lymphoma over a reactive process.

incorrectas.A: Bcl-6 is a germinal center marker expressed in both reactive germinal centers and FL, since it simply confirms germinal center derivation — it does not distinguish neoplastic from reactive follicles the way BCL2 does.
incorrectas.B: CD10 is likewise a germinal center B-cell marker present in both reactive centers and FL, useful for confirming germinal center origin but not for telling malignant from reactive processes apart.
incorrectas.C: Ki-67, a proliferation marker, is typically high in actively proliferating reactive germinal centers and often lower in the low-grade, slower-dividing FL, meaning its pattern actually runs opposite to what one might naively expect for a malignancy, and it is not the classic diagnostic feature used here.

preguntas.q: Follicular lymphoma is distinguished from reactive follicular hyperplasia by which feature of the B-cell population within the follicles?

e.correcta: FL arises from a single transformed B-cell clone, with all neoplastic cells sharing an identical immunoglobulin gene rearrangement and the same light chain (all kappa or all lambda) — reflecting its true neoplastic origin. This monoclonality can be confirmed by flow cytometry (light chain restriction) or molecular clonality studies, in contrast to the polyclonal, physiologic response seen in reactive hyperplasia.

incorrectas.B: Polyclonality describes reactive hyperplasia, where follicles contain a mixed B-cell population responding to diverse antigens with both kappa and lambda light chains represented, not FL.
incorrectas.C: FL B cells still express surface immunoglobulin (with light chain restriction); an actual absence of surface Ig would point toward a different developmental stage or malignancy, not the monoclonality that defines FL here.
incorrectas.D: Both reactive hyperplasia and FL are fundamentally B-cell follicular processes (T cells reside in the paracortex/interfollicular areas), so T-cell predominance does not discriminate between the two entities.

preguntas.q: Grade 1 follicular lymphoma is histologically defined by a predominance of which cell type?

e.correcta: FL grading is based on the number of centroblasts (large noncleaved cells) counted per high-power field. Grade 1 disease has few centroblasts and is dominated by small cleaved centrocytes, reflecting a more differentiated tumor with a lower proliferative rate — consistent with the general oncologic principle that better-differentiated tumors, closer to their normal cell of origin, tend to behave less aggressively.

incorrectas.A: A predominance of large noncleaved centroblasts instead defines the higher grades of FL (especially grade 3), which carry a worse prognosis and are sometimes managed more like an aggressive lymphoma.
incorrectas.C: Reed-Sternberg cells are diagnostic of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, an entirely separate disease entity, not part of the FL grading scheme.
incorrectas.D: Plasmacytoid lymphocytes are characteristic of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia, not a feature used in grading follicular lymphoma.

preguntas.q: Grade 2 follicular lymphoma is histologically characterized by which finding?

o.A: A pure population of small cleaved centrocytes
o.B: A pure population of large noncleaved centroblasts
o.C: A mixture of small cleaved centrocytes and large noncleaved centroblasts
o.D: Sheets of immunoblasts with no follicular pattern

e.correcta: FL grading exists along a continuum based on centroblast count per high-power field, with grade 2 falling between grade 1 (predominantly centrocytes) and grade 3 (predominantly centroblasts). This admixture of both cell types reflects an intermediate degree of differentiation and, correspondingly, an intermediate position on the aggressiveness spectrum.

incorrectas.A: A pure centrocyte population instead describes grade 1 FL, the lowest-grade, most indolent end of the spectrum.
incorrectas.B: A pure centroblast population describes grade 3 FL, the highest-grade, most aggressive end of the spectrum, which can behave more like diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: Sheets of immunoblasts with no follicular pattern describe a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma growth pattern, not a follicular lymphoma grade, since FL by definition retains a nodular/follicular architecture.

preguntas.q: Grade 3 follicular lymphoma is defined by a predominance of which cell type, correlating with a more aggressive clinical course?

e.correcta: Grade 3 FL has the highest centroblast (large noncleaved cell) count per high-power field among the FL grades, and grade 3B in particular (sheets of centroblasts) is often clinically managed like diffuse large B-cell lymphoma because of its greater aggressiveness and higher proliferative rate — illustrating how histologic grade in FL tracks with tumor behavior.

incorrectas.A: A predominance of centrocytes instead defines grade 1, the most indolent end of the FL grading spectrum — essentially the opposite of what is being asked.
incorrectas.B: Reed-Sternberg cells are the diagnostic cell of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, unrelated to the centroblast-based grading criteria used in FL.
incorrectas.C: Mast cells are not part of the FL grading system, which is based purely on centroblast quantity rather than on stromal or accessory immune cell infiltrates.

preguntas.q: Is follicular lymphoma typically an indolent or an aggressive lymphoma?

o.C: Rapidly fatal without treatment within weeks

e.correcta: FL is a low-grade, slow-growing (indolent) B-cell lymphoma; patients often have a prolonged, waxing-and-waning course over years, and treatment is deferred until symptoms develop, with watchful waiting standard for asymptomatic low-grade disease. The tradeoff of this indolent biology is that FL is notoriously difficult to cure outright, unlike many aggressive lymphomas that require immediate treatment but are more often curable.

incorrectas.B: Burkitt lymphoma is one of the fastest-growing human tumors, with a very high proliferative fraction requiring emergent treatment — FL sits at the opposite end of the aggressiveness spectrum among the NHLs.
incorrectas.C: Rapid fatality within weeks without treatment describes highly aggressive lymphomas such as Burkitt or lymphoblastic lymphoma, not FL, which can remain stable and asymptomatic for years untreated.
incorrectas.D: Acute leukemias (like ALL or AML) are rapidly progressive processes requiring urgent therapy — an entirely different tempo and biology from the chronic, indolent course of FL.

preguntas.q: Which demographic group is classically affected by mantle cell lymphoma?

e.correcta: Mantle cell lymphoma arises from naive, pre-germinal center B cells in the mantle zone surrounding a reactive follicle, and it classically affects older adult males (mnemonic: "man"tle). It often presents late, with widespread lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and GI tract involvement (lymphomatous polyposis) at the time of diagnosis.

incorrectas.B: Adult females are not the classic demographic; mantle cell lymphoma shows a clear male predominance rather than affecting women preferentially.
incorrectas.C: Elderly females predominantly describes the wrong sex distribution — the disease skews toward older men, not women, which is the basis of the "man"tle mnemonic.
incorrectas.D: Children of both sexes equally is incorrect because mantle cell lymphoma is a disease of older adults; pediatric-onset lymphomas of small B cells are not the typical presentation of this entity.

preguntas.q: The CCND1 gene, encoding cyclin D1 and translocated in mantle cell lymphoma via t(11;14), is normally located on which chromosome?

e.correcta: The t(11;14) translocation juxtaposes CCND1 (cyclin D1) on chromosome 11 with the strong IGH enhancer on chromosome 14, driving constitutive overexpression of cyclin D1. Cyclin D1 pushes cells through the G1/S checkpoint by inactivating Rb, producing the uncontrolled B-cell proliferation that defines mantle cell lymphoma.

incorrectas.A: Chromosome 14 is where the IGH enhancer sits — it is the translocation partner that drives overexpression, not the native location of the cyclin D1 gene itself.
incorrectas.C: Chromosome 8 houses the MYC oncogene, which is translocated in Burkitt lymphoma's t(8;14), a completely different lymphoma and translocation.
incorrectas.D: Chromosome 18 houses BCL2, involved in follicular lymphoma's t(14;18), not the cyclin D1 gene relevant to mantle cell lymphoma.

preguntas.q: How would you classify the clinical behavior of mantle cell lymphoma?

e.correcta: Despite histologically resembling small, mature-looking lymphocytes, mantle cell lymphoma behaves aggressively — it typically presents with late-stage, disseminated disease and carries a poor prognosis. This paradox (bland cytology, aggressive course) is driven by cyclin D1 overexpression pushing cells rapidly through the cell cycle.

incorrectas.A: Indolent describes lymphomas like follicular or marginal zone lymphoma that progress slowly over years; mantle cell lymphoma's rapid clinical course and poor prognosis contradict this classification.
incorrectas.B: Pre-malignant lesion is incorrect — mantle cell lymphoma is a fully invasive, malignant neoplasm, not a precursor state that has yet to become cancer.
incorrectas.D: A chronic, low-grade course describes true indolent lymphomas; mantle cell lymphoma's deceptively bland-appearing cells actually behave aggressively rather than following a slow, chronic trajectory.

preguntas.q: Which lymphoma is a neoplastic proliferation of small CD20+ B cells that expands into the marginal zone surrounding lymphoid follicles?

e.correcta: Marginal zone lymphoma is composed of small CD20+ B cells derived from post-germinal center (memory) B cells that expand into the marginal zone, the region just outside the mantle zone. It often arises in the setting of chronic antigenic stimulation and, when it occurs at mucosal sites, is termed a MALToma.

incorrectas.A: Mantle cell lymphoma expands the mantle zone surrounding the germinal center, not the marginal zone, and is driven by cyclin D1 overexpression from t(11;14) with a CD5+ phenotype, distinguishing it from marginal zone lymphoma.
incorrectas.B: Follicular lymphoma is composed of centrocytes and centroblasts arising within germinal center follicles themselves (driven by BCL2 overexpression from t(14;18)), not cells expanding the surrounding marginal zone.
incorrectas.C: CLL/SLL consists of small CD5+/CD23+ B cells that diffusely infiltrate lymph nodes and marrow rather than being confined to a specific anatomic zone like the marginal zone.

preguntas.q: Which B-cell lymphoma classically arises in the setting of chronic inflammatory or autoimmune conditions such as Hashimoto thyroiditis, Sjögren syndrome, or H. pylori gastritis?

e.correcta: Chronic antigenic stimulation from autoimmune disease or infection (Hashimoto thyroiditis, Sjögren syndrome, H. pylori gastritis) drives sustained B-cell proliferation in the marginal zone, which over time can become monoclonal marginal zone lymphoma. When this occurs at a mucosal site it is specifically called a MALToma, and removing the antigenic trigger (e.g., H. pylori eradication) can sometimes reverse early disease.

incorrectas.B: Burkitt lymphoma is driven by MYC translocation, with the endemic form linked to EBV infection rather than chronic autoimmune or inflammatory conditions like Hashimoto thyroiditis or Sjögren syndrome.
incorrectas.C: Mantle cell lymphoma is driven by cyclin D1 overexpression from t(11;14) and has no established association with chronic antigen-driven inflammatory states.
incorrectas.D: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by Reed-Sternberg cells recruiting a reactive infiltrate via cytokines, a different pathogenesis from the chronic-antigen-driven B-cell expansion that produces marginal zone lymphoma.

preguntas.q: What term describes marginal zone lymphoma arising specifically at mucosal sites, such as the stomach in the setting of chronic H. pylori infection?

e.correcta: A MALToma is marginal zone lymphoma arising in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, with gastric MALToma secondary to chronic H. pylori gastritis being the classic example. Because its growth is driven by ongoing antigenic stimulation, early-stage gastric MALToma can sometimes regress completely with H. pylori eradication therapy alone, without chemotherapy.

incorrectas.A: Burkitt lymphoma is an intermediate B-cell lymphoma driven by a MYC translocation, unrelated to the mucosal, antigen-driven origin that defines a MALToma.
incorrectas.C: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is composed of large, aggressive B cells growing diffusely; it is not the specific mucosal marginal zone entity tied to chronic inflammatory stimulation.
incorrectas.D: Follicular lymphoma arises from germinal center B cells with a BCL2 rearrangement and grows in a follicular pattern, distinct from the mucosal marginal zone origin of a MALToma.

preguntas.q: Which lymphoma is a neoplastic proliferation of intermediate-sized CD20+ B cells classically producing a "starry sky" histologic pattern?

e.correcta: Burkitt lymphoma consists of intermediate-sized, monomorphic CD20+ B cells with an extremely high proliferation rate (Ki-67 near 100%), driven by MYC dysregulation. The rapid turnover produces numerous apoptotic tumor cells that are ingested by tingible-body macrophages, creating pale "stars" scattered against the dark sheet of tumor cells — the classic starry sky pattern.

incorrectas.A: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is composed of large cells (nuclei at least 5x the size of a normal lymphocyte), not the intermediate-sized cells of Burkitt lymphoma, and does not classically show the same prominent starry sky pattern.
incorrectas.B: Mantle cell lymphoma consists of small-to-medium, monotonous lymphocytes expanding the mantle zone, lacking the very high proliferation rate and starry sky appearance characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: Marginal zone lymphoma is composed of small B cells with a much lower proliferation index, producing a very different, less mitotically active histologic picture than Burkitt lymphoma.

preguntas.q: Endemic (African) Burkitt lymphoma, which classically presents as a jaw mass in children, is strongly associated with infection by which virus?

e.correcta: EBV infects B cells and its latent gene products provide survival and proliferation signals that cooperate with the MYC translocation t(8;14) to drive endemic Burkitt lymphoma; nearly all endemic (jaw-form, African) cases are EBV-positive, compared with only a minority of sporadic cases. Chronic malaria in these regions is thought to impair immune control of EBV-infected B cells, further promoting lymphomagenesis.

incorrectas.A: CMV typically causes a mononucleosis-like illness or, in immunosuppressed patients, retinitis and colitis — it is not the virus classically linked to endemic Burkitt lymphoma.
incorrectas.B: HHV-8 causes Kaposi sarcoma, primary effusion lymphoma, and multicentric Castleman disease, a different set of B-cell and endothelial pathologies unrelated to Burkitt lymphoma.
incorrectas.C: HTLV-1 causes adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, a malignancy of T cells rather than the B-cell lineage affected in Burkitt lymphoma.

preguntas.q: Burkitt lymphoma classically presents as a rapidly growing extranodal mass in which age group(s)?

o.B: Infants under 1 year of age only

e.correcta: Burkitt lymphoma classically arises in children and young adults, presenting as a rapidly growing extranodal mass — the jaw in the endemic African form, or the abdomen/ileocecal region in the sporadic form. Its origin from highly proliferative germinal center B cells with near-100% Ki-67 index gives it one of the fastest doubling times of any human cancer, explaining the abrupt, dramatic presentation.

incorrectas.B: Infants under 1 year is too narrow and too young — Burkitt lymphoma typically affects somewhat older children and young adults rather than presenting in early infancy.
incorrectas.C: Middle-aged adults (40-60 years) is more characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which trends toward an older adult population rather than the childhood/young adult predominance of Burkitt lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: Elderly patients (over 70) is atypical for Burkitt lymphoma, which is predominantly a disease of childhood and young adulthood, not advanced age.

preguntas.q: The MYC oncogene, translocated in Burkitt lymphoma via t(8;14), is normally located on which chromosome?

e.correcta: MYC, the transcription factor gene translocated in Burkitt lymphoma's t(8;14), normally resides on chromosome 8. The translocation relocates MYC next to the powerful IGH enhancer on chromosome 14, causing constitutive MYC overexpression that drives unchecked cell cycle entry and the extremely rapid proliferation characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.

incorrectas.A: Chromosome 14 is the location of the IGH enhancer that drives MYC overexpression once translocated there — it is the translocation partner site, not the native MYC locus itself.
incorrectas.C: Chromosome 11 houses CCND1 (cyclin D1), involved in mantle cell lymphoma's t(11;14) translocation, a completely different lymphoma and gene.
incorrectas.D: Chromosome 18 houses BCL2, involved in follicular lymphoma's t(14;18) translocation, unrelated to the MYC gene relevant to Burkitt lymphoma.

preguntas.q: Which lymphoma is characterized by large CD20+ B cells growing diffusely in sheets, effacing the normal lymph node architecture?

e.correcta: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is defined by large, poorly differentiated CD20+ B cells — nuclei at least five times the size of a normal lymphocyte — that grow diffusely in sheets rather than forming organized follicles, obliterating the normal lymph node architecture. Because the cells express CD20, rituximab (anti-CD20 antibody) combined with chemotherapy (R-CHOP) is a mainstay of treatment.

incorrectas.A: Follicular lymphoma retains a nodular/follicular growth pattern composed of centrocytes and centroblasts arising within germinal centers, rather than diffuse sheets of large cells replacing the architecture.
incorrectas.B: Burkitt lymphoma is composed of intermediate-sized, monomorphic cells with a classic starry sky pattern — smaller and more uniform than the large, poorly differentiated cells that define DLBCL.
incorrectas.D: Mantle cell lymphoma consists of small-to-medium, monotonous lymphocytes expanding the mantle zone, not the large cells growing diffusely in sheets that characterize DLBCL.

preguntas.q: What is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma overall?

e.correcta: DLBCL is the single most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults. It also occurs at increased frequency in HIV-infected patients, where it is considered an AIDS-defining illness, reflecting impaired immune surveillance and chronic (often EBV-driven) B-cell stimulation that promotes malignant transformation.

incorrectas.A: Follicular lymphoma is the second most common NHL subtype — an indolent, low-grade lymphoma — but it does not surpass DLBCL in overall frequency.
incorrectas.B: Burkitt lymphoma is highly aggressive but comparatively rare overall, notable mainly in specific populations (endemic pediatric cases, immunocompromised adults), not as the most common NHL subtype.
incorrectas.C: Marginal zone lymphoma is a relatively uncommon, indolent NHL subtype arising from chronic antigenic stimulation, occurring far less frequently than DLBCL.

preguntas.q: DLBCL is clinically classified as which type of lymphoma?

e.correcta: DLBCL is clinically aggressive — its large, poorly differentiated tumor cells proliferate rapidly, and untreated disease progresses quickly, often requiring urgent initiation of chemoimmunotherapy. Paradoxically, this same aggressiveness makes DLBCL potentially curable with regimens like R-CHOP, whereas some indolent lymphomas, despite growing slowly, are actually harder to eradicate completely.

incorrectas.B: Indolent describes slow-growing lymphomas such as follicular or marginal zone lymphoma; DLBCL's rapid growth and need for prompt treatment are the opposite of this behavior.
incorrectas.C: Low-grade histology refers to small, well-differentiated cells with slow turnover; DLBCL's large, poorly differentiated cells and high proliferation rate instead define it as high-grade/aggressive.
incorrectas.D: Pre-malignant would imply a precursor state rather than an established cancer — DLBCL is a fully invasive malignant lymphoma, not a premalignant condition.

preguntas.q: DLBCL may arise de novo or through histologic transformation of which low-grade lymphoma?

e.correcta: DLBCL can arise sporadically or through transformation of a pre-existing low-grade lymphoma, most classically follicular lymphoma (transformation from CLL/SLL, called Richter transformation, is another well-known example). Additional genetic hits — such as MYC or TP53 alterations layered onto the existing BCL2 rearrangement — push the indolent centrocytes/centroblasts toward a more aggressive, large-cell phenotype.

incorrectas.A: Hodgkin lymphoma is a distinct entity driven by Reed-Sternberg cells arising from a different pathogenic pathway; it does not transform into DLBCL, which belongs to a separate lymphoma lineage.
incorrectas.C: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm, not a low-grade lymphocytic lymphoma capable of transforming into DLBCL.
incorrectas.D: Burkitt lymphoma is itself aggressive from onset (driven by MYC translocation) rather than being a low-grade precursor lymphoma that transforms into DLBCL over time.

preguntas.q: DLBCL most commonly presents in which age group as an enlarging lymph node or extranodal mass?

e.correcta: DLBCL most commonly presents in late adulthood, consistent with the accumulation of genetic alterations (BCL2, BCL6, MYC dysregulation) over decades of B-cell turnover. Presentation can be nodal (an enlarging lymph node) or extranodal, with sites including the GI tract, skin, bone, and CNS.

incorrectas.A: Early childhood is far more typical of Burkitt lymphoma or precursor lymphoblastic lymphomas than of DLBCL, which trends toward an older population.
incorrectas.B: Adolescence is not the typical peak for DLBCL; while Hodgkin lymphoma has a bimodal age distribution that includes young adulthood, DLBCL skews toward older adults.
incorrectas.D: The neonatal period is essentially never the presentation age for DLBCL, since it requires the accumulation of oncogenic mutations over a much longer lifespan.

preguntas.q: Approximately what percentage of DLBCL cases occur in children, despite the disease usually presenting in older adults?

e.correcta: Although DLBCL is predominantly a disease of older adults, roughly 20% of cases occur in children. This is a reminder that age alone cannot exclude the diagnosis; pediatric DLBCL also tends to have different molecular subtypes and generally better treatment outcomes than adult-onset disease.

incorrectas.A: 5% underestimates the actual pediatric proportion, which is meaningfully higher — closer to one-fifth of all DLBCL cases.
incorrectas.B: 50% would imply DLBCL occurs equally in children and adults, which contradicts its clear predominance in older adult populations.
incorrectas.C: 80% would suggest DLBCL is primarily a pediatric disease, the opposite of its true epidemiology, which is weighted toward late adulthood.

preguntas.q: Primary CNS lymphoma, an AIDS-defining illness, is most commonly seen in patients with which underlying condition?

e.correcta: Primary CNS lymphoma is an AIDS-defining illness and the most common CNS tumor in immunosuppressed patients. It arises from EBV-driven B-cell proliferation that escapes immune surveillance when CD4 counts are severely depleted (typically below 50 cells/µL), and its incidence has declined substantially with widespread antiretroviral therapy.

incorrectas.B: Diabetes mellitus causes vascular and neuropathic complications but does not produce the profound immunosuppression that predisposes to EBV-driven primary CNS lymphoma.
incorrectas.C: Chronic hepatitis C is associated with mixed cryoglobulinemia and certain peripheral B-cell lymphomas, but it is not classically linked to primary CNS lymphoma the way HIV/AIDS is.
incorrectas.D: Sarcoidosis is a granulomatous inflammatory disease that can itself affect the CNS (neurosarcoidosis), but it does not predispose to primary CNS lymphoma.

preguntas.q: Which CNS neoplasm typically presents in adults with confusion, memory loss, and seizures, and is strongly associated with immunosuppression?

e.correcta: Primary CNS lymphoma presents with variable neurologic findings — confusion, memory loss, seizures — depending on lesion location, reflecting diffuse infiltration of malignant B lymphocytes with characteristic perivascular cuffing around brain vessels. It should be strongly suspected in an immunosuppressed patient (especially advanced HIV/AIDS) presenting with a new brain mass.

incorrectas.A: Glioblastoma multiforme also causes focal deficits and seizures, but it arises from glial cells rather than lymphocytes and is not specifically tied to immunosuppression or EBV infection the way primary CNS lymphoma is.
incorrectas.C: Meningioma is usually slow-growing, often incidental, and causes symptoms from mass effect on adjacent brain structures; it typically occurs in immunocompetent patients (often older women), not in the setting of immunosuppression.
incorrectas.D: Metastatic carcinoma originates from a systemic epithelial primary (e.g., lung, breast) that spreads to brain — an entirely different pathogenesis from the EBV-driven B-cell lymphoproliferation of primary CNS lymphoma.

preguntas.q: On MRI, primary CNS lymphoma classically appears as what kind of lesion, in contrast to the multiple ring-enhancing lesions of toxoplasmosis?

o.D: A single cystic lesion with a fluid level

e.correcta: Primary CNS lymphoma classically appears as a single, solid, often periventricular lesion on MRI (though multifocal disease can occur), which helps distinguish it from CNS toxoplasmosis, which typically produces multiple ring-enhancing lesions. This imaging distinction is a key first step in narrowing the differential in an HIV-positive patient with a new brain mass.

incorrectas.A: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions is the classic appearance of CNS toxoplasmosis, not primary CNS lymphoma, and is precisely the finding used to distinguish toxoplasmosis from lymphoma on imaging.
incorrectas.B: Multiple calcified lesions are more characteristic of chronic granulomatous or parasitic processes such as neurocysticercosis, not the typical acute imaging pattern of either lymphoma or toxoplasmosis.
incorrectas.D: A single cystic lesion with a fluid level suggests a brain abscess with liquefactive necrosis, a different pathologic process from the solid mass typical of primary CNS lymphoma.

preguntas.q: In an HIV-positive patient with a brain mass, primary CNS lymphoma must be distinguished from which infectious mimicker using CSF analysis or additional testing?

e.correcta: Primary CNS lymphoma must be distinguished from toxoplasmosis in HIV-positive patients, since both occur in advanced immunosuppression and can appear clinically similar. CSF analysis (EBV PCR favoring lymphoma versus Toxoplasma serology/PCR favoring toxoplasmosis) or a trial of empiric anti-toxoplasma therapy with repeat imaging in 1-2 weeks is used to differentiate the two.

incorrectas.A: Cryptococcosis typically presents with meningitis — headache and elevated CSF opening pressure — diagnosed via CSF cryptococcal antigen, rather than as a discrete mass lesion mimicking lymphoma.
incorrectas.B: PML is caused by JC virus reactivation and produces non-enhancing white matter lesions without significant mass effect, a very different imaging and clinical picture from the enhancing mass lesions of lymphoma or toxoplasmosis.
incorrectas.C: CMV encephalitis causes a diffuse encephalitis/ventriculitis pattern in advanced AIDS rather than the discrete mass lesion that requires differentiation from lymphoma the way toxoplasmosis does.

preguntas.q: Reed-Sternberg cells in classical Hodgkin lymphoma are classically positive for which two surface markers?

e.correcta: Reed-Sternberg cells, though derived from germinal center B cells, characteristically express CD15 and CD30 while typically losing CD20 — a distinctive immunophenotype used to diagnose classical Hodgkin lymphoma. The mnemonic "2 owl eyes x 15 = 30" ties the binucleated, owl-eye nuclear morphology to these two markers.

incorrectas.B: CD20 and CD79a are pan-B-cell markers retained in most B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas, but classical Reed-Sternberg cells characteristically lose CD20 expression, making this combination atypical rather than diagnostic for Hodgkin lymphoma.
incorrectas.C: CD3 and CD5 are T-cell markers; Reed-Sternberg cells are of B-cell origin despite their atypical marker loss, so a T-cell immunophenotype would not fit this diagnosis.
incorrectas.D: CD10 and CD19 mark germinal center B cells (as seen in follicular lymphoma or Burkitt lymphoma) and pan-B-cell lineage respectively, but Reed-Sternberg cells lose most conventional B-cell markers rather than retaining this pairing.

preguntas.q: Reed-Sternberg cells drive much of the reactive inflammatory infiltrate and systemic symptoms of Hodgkin lymphoma by secreting which class of signaling molecules?

e.correcta: Reed-Sternberg cells secrete a broad array of cytokines (including IL-5, IL-6, and TNF-alpha) that recruit and activate the reactive infiltrate of eosinophils, plasma cells, lymphocytes, and macrophages surrounding the relatively sparse malignant cells. This cytokine-driven recruitment explains why Hodgkin lymphoma tumors are composed mostly of reactive cells rather than the malignant clone itself.

incorrectas.A: Immunoglobulin secretion is a function of normal, differentiated B cells and plasma cells, but Reed-Sternberg cells have largely lost B-cell differentiation programs and are not defined by antibody production driving the tumor microenvironment.
incorrectas.C: Complement proteins are produced mainly by the liver and various immune cells as part of innate immunity, not the signaling molecules Reed-Sternberg cells use to recruit the surrounding inflammatory infiltrate.
incorrectas.D: Prostaglandins alone underrepresents the actual biology — Reed-Sternberg cells secrete a broad cytokine profile (IL-5, IL-6, TNF-alpha, etc.) that is responsible for both the reactive infiltrate and the systemic B symptoms, not prostaglandins in isolation.

preguntas.q: Fever, chills, weight loss, and night sweats resulting from Reed-Sternberg cell cytokine secretion in Hodgkin lymphoma are collectively known as what?

e.correcta: Fever, chills, weight loss, and night sweats driven by Reed-Sternberg cell cytokine secretion are termed "B" symptoms. Their presence upstages a patient's Ann Arbor stage (for example, stage IIA becomes IIB), signaling greater systemic tumor burden and a worse prognosis.

incorrectas.A: Sézary syndrome is a leukemic variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides) presenting with erythroderma and circulating atypical T cells, unrelated to Hodgkin lymphoma's constitutional symptom complex.
incorrectas.B: Cytokine release syndrome is a distinct acute toxicity associated with CAR-T cell therapy or certain immunotherapies, not the chronic constitutional symptom pattern of Hodgkin lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: SIRS describes a general physiologic response to a severe insult like sepsis or trauma, defined by specific vital sign and lab criteria, not the specific staging-relevant symptom complex of Hodgkin lymphoma.

preguntas.q: The bulk of the tumor mass in Hodgkin lymphoma is composed of which cell population?

e.correcta: In Hodgkin lymphoma, the actual malignant Reed-Sternberg cells make up only a small minority of the tumor mass; the bulk consists of a reactive inflammatory infiltrate — lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells, and macrophages — recruited by Reed-Sternberg cell cytokine secretion. The composition and pattern of this background infiltrate forms the basis for histologic subclassification (nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted).

incorrectas.A: The malignant Reed-Sternberg cells are actually rare within the tumor mass, making this option the opposite of the true histologic composition despite being the cell type that defines the diagnosis.
incorrectas.B: Neoplastic small lymphocytes describes entities like CLL/SLL; in Hodgkin lymphoma the small lymphocytes present in the tumor are reactive bystanders, not the malignant clone.
incorrectas.C: Metastatic epithelial cells would indicate carcinoma metastatic to a lymph node, an entirely different disease process unrelated to the lymphoid origin of Hodgkin lymphoma.

preguntas.q: What is the most common histologic subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma, accounting for about 70% of cases?

e.correcta: Nodular sclerosis is the most common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma (about 70% of cases), characterized by broad bands of collagen dividing the lymph node into nodules and lacunar-type Reed-Sternberg cell variants. It tends to affect young adults, including a relative female predominance, and typically carries a good prognosis with a comparatively slower-growing course.

incorrectas.B: Mixed cellularity is the second most common subtype, featuring an eosinophil- and lymphocyte-rich mixed infiltrate and a stronger association with EBV and HIV infection, but it does not surpass nodular sclerosis in frequency.
incorrectas.C: Lymphocyte-rich is a less common subtype with abundant reactive lymphocytes and relatively few Reed-Sternberg cells, generally carrying a favorable prognosis but occurring far less often than nodular sclerosis.
incorrectas.D: Lymphocyte-depleted is the rarest and most aggressive subtype, seen more often in elderly or immunocompromised (e.g., HIV-positive) patients, and is not the predominant subtype in the general population.

preguntas.q: The nodular sclerosis subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma, the most common subtype overall, is classically associated with which demographic group?

e.correcta: Nodular sclerosis is the single most common subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma and is the notable exception to the general male predominance of Hodgkin disease, occurring most often in young adult (often adolescent to 30s) women. Histologically it shows broad bands of fibrosis dividing the node into nodules and characteristic lacunar-type Reed-Sternberg cells, and it commonly presents with a mediastinal mass.

incorrectas.A: Elderly men is the demographic linked to the lymphocyte-depleted subtype (and to Hodgkin's second age peak generally), not nodular sclerosis; lymphocyte-depleted disease is aggressive and carries the worst prognosis, unlike the favorable nodular sclerosis form.
incorrectas.C: Male children under 10 do not typify Hodgkin lymphoma, which has a bimodal age distribution peaking in young adults and again after 55; nodular sclerosis specifically clusters in young adults rather than young children.
incorrectas.D: HIV-positive middle-aged men are associated with the lymphocyte-depleted subtype and with more aggressive, immunosuppression-related Hodgkin disease, whereas nodular sclerosis arises in otherwise healthy young women and is not driven by HIV.

preguntas.q: Which subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma carries the best prognosis?

e.correcta: For Hodgkin lymphoma the general rule is that the more reactive lymphocytes present relative to Reed-Sternberg cells, the better the prognosis. The lymphocyte-rich subtype therefore has the most favorable outcome, reflecting a robust host immune response and a low tumor cell burden.

incorrectas.A: Mixed cellularity has an intermediate prognosis and shows a mix of Reed-Sternberg cells with eosinophils, plasma cells, and lymphocytes; its higher RS-cell content and eosinophil-rich background make it less favorable than the lymphocyte-rich form.
incorrectas.B: Nodular sclerosis has a good but not the best prognosis; while common and generally treatable, it is defined by fibrous banding rather than the lymphocyte predominance that confers the most favorable outcome.
incorrectas.D: Lymphocyte-depleted has the worst prognosis of the classical subtypes because abundant Reed-Sternberg cells with scant reactive lymphocytes signal an aggressive tumor and weak immune response, the opposite of the lymphocyte-rich pattern.

preguntas.q: A lymph node biopsy in a patient with Hodgkin lymphoma shows Reed-Sternberg cells within a background rich in eosinophils, plasma cells, and lymphocytes. Which subtype is most consistent with these findings?

e.correcta: Mixed cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by a heterogeneous inflammatory background containing abundant eosinophils, plasma cells, and lymphocytes intermixed with numerous Reed-Sternberg cells. The eosinophilia is driven by IL-5 secreted by the Reed-Sternberg cells, and this subtype is often associated with EBV and can present with prominent B symptoms.

incorrectas.A: Nodular sclerosis is instead characterized by dense collagen bands dividing the node and lacunar-type Reed-Sternberg cells, not by an eosinophil-rich inflammatory milieu as the defining feature.
incorrectas.C: Lymphocyte-rich disease is dominated by a background of small reactive lymphocytes with relatively few Reed-Sternberg cells and lacks the prominent eosinophil and plasma cell infiltrate seen in mixed cellularity.
incorrectas.D: Lymphocyte-depleted disease shows abundant Reed-Sternberg cells with a sparse reactive background, essentially the opposite of the lymphocyte- and eosinophil-rich pattern that defines mixed cellularity.

preguntas.q: Eosinophilia in Hodgkin lymphoma, particularly the mixed cellularity subtype, is driven by which cytokine secreted by Reed-Sternberg cells?

e.correcta: IL-5 is the key cytokine that promotes eosinophil growth, differentiation, and recruitment, so Reed-Sternberg cell secretion of IL-5 explains the eosinophil-rich background of Hodgkin lymphoma, especially the mixed cellularity subtype. Recognizing IL-5 as the eosinophil-driving cytokine is high-yield and also underlies eosinophilia in allergic and parasitic conditions.

incorrectas.A: IL-2 is a T-cell growth factor that drives proliferation of T lymphocytes and NK cells; it does not selectively expand the eosinophil lineage the way IL-5 does.
incorrectas.C: IL-6 is produced in multiple myeloma to stimulate plasma cell growth and also drives acute-phase reactants and fever, but it is not the cytokine responsible for eosinophilia in Hodgkin lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: IL-12 promotes Th1 differentiation and activates NK and cytotoxic T cells; it has no direct role in stimulating eosinophil production, unlike IL-5.

preguntas.q: Which subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma is the most aggressive?

e.correcta: Lymphocyte-depleted Hodgkin lymphoma is the most aggressive classical subtype and carries the worst prognosis, consistent with the principle that fewer reactive lymphocytes relative to Reed-Sternberg cells signals a worse outcome. It is disproportionately seen in the elderly and in HIV-positive/immunocompromised patients and often presents at an advanced stage.

incorrectas.B: Lymphocyte-rich disease is at the opposite end of the spectrum, with abundant reactive lymphocytes and the best prognosis, making it far less aggressive than lymphocyte-depleted disease.
incorrectas.C: Nodular sclerosis is a common, generally favorable subtype in young women; while it can present with bulky mediastinal disease, it is not the most aggressive form.
incorrectas.D: Mixed cellularity has an intermediate prognosis and, although it can be associated with disseminated disease, it is less aggressive than the lymphocyte-depleted subtype.

preguntas.q: An older, HIV-positive man is diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma that is aggressive and carries a poor prognosis. Which subtype is most likely?

e.correcta: Lymphocyte-depleted Hodgkin lymphoma is classically seen in elderly and HIV-positive/immunosuppressed patients and has the worst prognosis of the classical subtypes. Its abundance of Reed-Sternberg cells with a scant reactive lymphocyte background reflects both an aggressive tumor and a poor host immune response, fitting the general rule that fewer lymphocytes means worse outcome.

incorrectas.A: Nodular sclerosis occurs in young women and has a favorable prognosis, the opposite demographic and behavior of the aggressive disease described in an elderly HIV-positive man.
incorrectas.B: Lymphocyte-rich disease carries the best prognosis and is not the subtype linked to immunosuppression or advanced age, so it does not fit an aggressive, poor-outcome presentation.
incorrectas.D: Mixed cellularity is EBV-associated and can occur in immunocompromised patients, but it has an intermediate prognosis and is not classically the elderly/HIV-linked subtype with the worst outcome, which is lymphocyte-depleted.

preguntas.q: Most subtypes of Hodgkin lymphoma show a predominance in which group, with nodular sclerosis being the notable exception?

e.correcta: Hodgkin lymphoma overall shows a male predominance, and this holds for most subtypes such as mixed cellularity and lymphocyte-depleted. The important exception is nodular sclerosis, which occurs more often in young women, a distinction frequently tested on Step 1.

incorrectas.A: Women are specifically the group in which nodular sclerosis predominates, but nodular sclerosis is the exception rather than the rule; the other subtypes are more common in men.
incorrectas.C: Children are not the group in which most Hodgkin subtypes predominate; Hodgkin lymphoma has a bimodal peak in young adults and older adults rather than a childhood male-vs-female skew.
incorrectas.D: The elderly represent the second age peak and are linked to the lymphocyte-depleted subtype, but age is a separate axis from the sex predominance being asked about, which favors men.

preguntas.q: A lymphoma in which the tumor mass is composed predominantly of neoplastic lymphoid cells (mostly of B-cell lineage) rather than reactive inflammatory cells is best described as which type?

e.correcta: In non-Hodgkin lymphoma the tumor mass is made up largely of the malignant lymphoid cells themselves, the vast majority of which are B cells (with a minority of T-cell lineage such as adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma). This contrasts sharply with Hodgkin lymphoma, where the actual neoplastic Reed-Sternberg cells are rare and the bulk of the mass is reactive inflammatory cells.

incorrectas.A: Hodgkin lymphoma masses are composed mostly of reactive inflammatory cells with only scattered malignant Reed-Sternberg cells, the opposite of a mass built from the neoplastic lymphoid cells themselves.
incorrectas.C: Reactive follicular hyperplasia is a benign, non-neoplastic response to antigenic stimulation and does not represent a clonal lymphoid malignancy at all.
incorrectas.D: Mixed cellularity is a subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma and is specifically rich in reactive eosinophils, plasma cells, and lymphocytes, so it does not describe a mass composed of neoplastic lymphoid cells.

preguntas.q: A lymph node biopsy shows only rare malignant cells scattered within a mass composed predominantly of reactive inflammatory cells. This histologic pattern is characteristic of which type of lymphoma?

e.correcta: Hodgkin lymphoma is distinctive in that the neoplastic Reed-Sternberg cells make up only a small fraction of the tumor, while the bulk of the mass consists of reactive inflammatory cells (lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells, histiocytes) recruited by cytokines the RS cells secrete. This heavy reactive infiltrate is a defining contrast with non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

incorrectas.A: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma masses are composed mostly of the neoplastic lymphoid cells themselves, not a predominance of reactive inflammatory cells surrounding rare tumor cells.
incorrectas.C: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a non-Hodgkin B-cell neoplasm in which the tumor cells (small mature lymphocytes) themselves dominate the blood, marrow, and nodes, rather than a reactive-cell-rich mass.
incorrectas.D: Burkitt lymphoma is an aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma with sheets of monomorphic neoplastic B cells and a starry-sky pattern from tingible-body macrophages, not a background dominated by reactive inflammatory cells.

preguntas.q: Which type of lymphoma classically spreads in an orderly, contiguous fashion from one group of lymph nodes to the next and is only rarely extranodal?

e.correcta: Hodgkin lymphoma characteristically arises in a single localized group of nodes and spreads in a predictable, contiguous fashion to adjacent nodal groups, with extranodal involvement being uncommon. This orderly spread is one reason Hodgkin disease is often diagnosed at a more localized stage and is amenable to staging-directed radiation.

incorrectas.B: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma spreads non-contiguously and unpredictably, often with widespread or diffuse involvement and more frequent extranodal disease, in contrast to the stepwise nodal spread of Hodgkin lymphoma.
incorrectas.C: The two are explicitly distinguished by their spread patterns: Hodgkin is contiguous and Non-Hodgkin is non-contiguous, so they do not behave identically.
incorrectas.D: Both lymphomas do involve lymph nodes; the distinction is the pattern of spread, not whether nodes are involved at all.

preguntas.q: Which type of lymphoma is characterized by non-contiguous, diffuse spread throughout the lymphatic system?

e.correcta: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma typically spreads in a non-contiguous, diffuse manner, jumping between non-adjacent nodal groups and frequently involving extranodal sites. This unpredictable dissemination often leads to more widespread disease at presentation compared with the orderly nodal progression of Hodgkin lymphoma.

incorrectas.A: Hodgkin lymphoma spreads contiguously from one nodal group to the next and is only rarely extranodal, the opposite of the diffuse, non-contiguous pattern described.
incorrectas.C: Only Hodgkin lymphoma spreads contiguously; non-Hodgkin lymphoma does not, so the claim that both spread contiguously is incorrect.
incorrectas.D: Both types clearly involve lymph nodes; the distinguishing feature is the diffuse versus stepwise pattern of spread.

preguntas.q: Extranodal involvement at presentation is more characteristic of which type of lymphoma?

e.correcta: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is much more likely to involve extranodal sites such as the GI tract, skin, CNS, and other organs, in keeping with its diffuse, non-contiguous spread. Hodgkin lymphoma, by contrast, tends to remain within contiguous nodal groups and only rarely involves extranodal tissue.

incorrectas.A: Hodgkin lymphoma is characteristically localized to nodal groups with only rare extranodal spread, so it is not the type associated with prominent extranodal disease.
incorrectas.C: The two differ meaningfully: extranodal involvement is a hallmark of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, not a shared feature of equal frequency.
incorrectas.D: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma frequently arises in or spreads to extranodal sites, so neither type being strictly nodal is false.

preguntas.q: In addition to chemotherapy regimens such as ABVD, what modality is a mainstay of treatment for localized Hodgkin lymphoma?

e.correcta: Because Hodgkin lymphoma spreads contiguously and is often localized at diagnosis, radiation therapy is a mainstay of treatment, frequently combined with chemotherapy such as ABVD (Adriamycin/doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, dacarbazine). A key testable complication is that radiation to the neck can cause iatrogenic hypothyroidism, and radiation near the head can cause hypopituitarism, along with a later risk of secondary malignancies.

incorrectas.B: Splenectomy is not a treatment modality for Hodgkin lymphoma; historically the spleen was assessed at staging laparotomy, but the disease is treated with radiation and chemotherapy, not surgical removal.
incorrectas.C: Autologous stem cell transplant is reserved for relapsed or refractory disease, not the initial mainstay for typical localized Hodgkin lymphoma.
incorrectas.D: Rituximab targets CD20, which classical Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells generally do not express, so rituximab monotherapy is not a standard mainstay for classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

preguntas.q: What is the most common PRIMARY malignancy of bone in adults over 40 to 50 years of age?

e.correcta: Multiple myeloma is the most common primary malignancy arising within bone in older adults; it is a clonal proliferation of plasma cells in the marrow that produces punched-out lytic lesions and bone pain. Note the careful distinction: metastatic cancer is the most common bone malignancy overall, but among primary bone malignancies in this age group, myeloma leads.

incorrectas.A: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor of adolescents and young adults, typically at the metaphysis of long bones near the knee, not the leading primary bone malignancy in older adults.
incorrectas.C: Chondrosarcoma is a cartilage-forming malignancy of middle-aged and older adults but is far less common than myeloma and typically affects the axial skeleton and pelvis.
incorrectas.D: Ewing sarcoma is an aggressive small round blue cell tumor of children and adolescents associated with the t(11;22) translocation, not a malignancy of adults over 40 to 50.

preguntas.q: What is the most common malignancy involving bone overall?

e.correcta: Metastatic disease is by far the most common malignancy found in bone, vastly outnumbering all primary bone tumors combined. Common primaries that metastasize to bone include breast, prostate, lung, thyroid, and kidney, and lesions may be lytic, blastic, or mixed.

incorrectas.A: Multiple myeloma is the most common PRIMARY malignancy of bone in older adults, but as a category primary bone malignancies are dwarfed by metastatic lesions.
incorrectas.C: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary bone SARCOMA and predominantly affects young patients, but it is uncommon relative to the frequency of metastatic bone disease.
incorrectas.D: Primary bone lymphoma is a rare entity; lymphoma far more often involves bone secondarily, and it does not approach the frequency of metastatic cancer overall.

preguntas.q: Multiple myeloma is associated with elevated serum levels of which cytokine, which stimulates plasma cell growth and immunoglobulin production?

e.correcta: IL-6 is a key growth factor for plasma cells and drives their proliferation and immunoglobulin secretion, so high serum IL-6 is characteristic of multiple myeloma and correlates with disease activity. IL-6 also functions as an acute-phase cytokine, which helps explain its broad pro-inflammatory role.

incorrectas.A: IL-5 stimulates eosinophil production and is the cytokine behind eosinophilia in Hodgkin lymphoma, not the plasma cell growth factor central to multiple myeloma.
incorrectas.C: TNF-alpha contributes to bone resorption and cachexia and may play an accessory role in the marrow microenvironment, but IL-6 is the cytokine classically cited as driving plasma cell proliferation in myeloma.
incorrectas.D: IL-10 is an anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses Th1 responses and macrophage activation; it is not the growth factor that expands the malignant plasma cell clone.

preguntas.q: How is the total serum protein level typically affected in multiple myeloma?

e.correcta: Serum total protein is typically elevated in multiple myeloma because the malignant plasma cell clone overproduces a monoclonal immunoglobulin (paraprotein). This excess protein manifests as the M spike on serum protein electrophoresis and contributes to findings such as an increased serum protein gap and rouleaux formation.

incorrectas.A: Decreased total protein is the wrong direction; although normal (polyclonal) immunoglobulins may actually fall, the massive monoclonal paraprotein production raises the total serum protein.
incorrectas.C: The total protein is not unchanged, since the clonal immunoglobulin overproduction shifts it upward, which is a core diagnostic clue prompting SPEP.
incorrectas.D: Serum protein is never undetectable; albumin and other proteins remain present, and in myeloma the paraprotein adds substantially to the total.

preguntas.q: Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) in multiple myeloma classically demonstrates which finding?

e.correcta: Multiple myeloma produces a sharp monoclonal (M) spike on SPEP, reflecting a single clone of plasma cells secreting one identical immunoglobulin. The M stands for monoclonal, and the spike usually appears in the gamma region, though it indicates a monoclonal gamma globulin rather than IgG specifically.

incorrectas.A: A broad-based polyclonal gammopathy reflects a reactive, non-neoplastic increase in many different immunoglobulins (as in chronic infection or inflammation), the opposite of the narrow monoclonal spike of myeloma.
incorrectas.C: A decreased albumin peak is not the diagnostic hallmark of myeloma; the defining SPEP feature is the addition of a discrete monoclonal spike in the globulin region.
incorrectas.D: An absent gamma region would suggest hypogammaglobulinemia; myeloma instead adds a tall, narrow monoclonal peak, not an absence of gamma globulins.

preguntas.q: What is the most common cause of death in patients with multiple myeloma?

e.correcta: Infection is the leading cause of death in multiple myeloma. Even though total immunoglobulin is high, it is all non-functional monoclonal paraprotein, and normal polyclonal antibody production is suppressed, leaving patients with a functional immunodeficiency; encapsulated organisms such as S. pneumoniae are particularly dangerous.

incorrectas.B: Renal failure (myeloma kidney) is a major and common complication from light chain cast nephropathy and hypercalcemia, but it is not the single most common cause of death, which is infection.
incorrectas.C: Pathologic fractures from lytic bone lesions cause significant morbidity and pain but are generally not the primary cause of mortality in myeloma.
incorrectas.D: Hypercalcemia from osteolysis can precipitate acute crises and contribute to renal injury, yet it is a manifestation and complication rather than the leading cause of death, which remains infection.

preguntas.q: A peripheral blood smear from a patient with multiple myeloma shows red blood cells stacked together like a column of poker chips. This finding is termed:

e.correcta: Rouleaux formation refers to red blood cells aligning in stacks resembling poker chips, and it occurs in multiple myeloma because the high concentration of monoclonal protein reduces the normal repulsive negative surface charge between RBCs, allowing them to aggregate. It is a classic smear clue that accompanies an elevated serum protein and ESR.

incorrectas.B: Schistocytes are fragmented red cells seen in microangiopathic hemolytic anemias such as DIC, TTP, or HUS from mechanical shearing, not stacked RBCs from excess paraprotein.
incorrectas.C: Spherocytes are small, round RBCs lacking central pallor seen in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia, a morphology unrelated to the stacking caused by high serum protein.
incorrectas.D: Basophilic stippling reflects aggregated ribosomes seen in lead poisoning, thalassemias, and sideroblastic anemia, not the aggregation of whole cells characteristic of rouleaux.

preguntas.q: In multiple myeloma, filtered free light chains (Bence Jones protein) deposit in the renal tubules, placing the patient at greatest risk for which complication?

e.correcta: Excess monoclonal free light chains are filtered and precipitate in the distal tubules as large eosinophilic casts, causing tubular obstruction and injury known as myeloma cast nephropathy or myeloma kidney, a leading cause of renal failure in myeloma. Because these are light chains rather than albumin, a standard urine dipstick (which detects albumin) is often negative despite heavy proteinuria.

incorrectas.B: Renal artery stenosis is a vascular narrowing causing renovascular hypertension and is unrelated to light chain deposition in tubules.
incorrectas.C: Minimal change disease is a podocyte disorder causing selective albumin loss and nephrotic syndrome, typically in children, not a tubular cast nephropathy from Bence Jones protein.
incorrectas.D: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is an immune-complex glomerular disease following streptococcal infection, a nephritic process mechanistically distinct from light chain cast nephropathy.

preguntas.q: An asymptomatic older patient is found to have an M spike on SPEP but has no CRAB features and no hyperviscosity symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

e.correcta: MGUS is defined by a monoclonal spike on SPEP in an asymptomatic patient who lacks the end-organ features of myeloma (no CRAB: hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions) and lacks the hyperviscosity of Waldenstrom. It is essentially a premalignant plasma cell condition that requires monitoring rather than treatment.

incorrectas.A: Multiple myeloma requires evidence of end-organ damage (CRAB features) or defining biomarkers in addition to the paraprotein, which by definition are absent in this asymptomatic patient.
incorrectas.C: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia produces a monoclonal IgM and causes hyperviscosity symptoms; the absence of hyperviscosity here argues against it.
incorrectas.D: Amyloidosis (AL type) involves light chain deposition causing organ dysfunction such as nephrotic syndrome, restrictive cardiomyopathy, or neuropathy, none of which fit a purely asymptomatic M spike.

preguntas.q: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is most commonly found in which age group?

e.correcta: MGUS is a disease of older adults, found in roughly 5% of individuals around age 70, and its prevalence rises with age. It is typically discovered incidentally and carries about a 1-2% per year risk of progressing to multiple myeloma or a related plasma cell malignancy.

incorrectas.A: Neonates do not develop MGUS; plasma cell dyscrasias reflect accumulated clonal mutations over a lifetime and are essentially unheard of at birth.
incorrectas.B: Adolescents are not the population affected by MGUS, which is strongly age-dependent and clusters in later decades of life.
incorrectas.C: Young adults occasionally have plasma cell disorders but MGUS specifically becomes common only in the elderly, so young adulthood is not the typical age group.

preguntas.q: Approximately 1-2% of patients with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) progress each year to which condition?

e.correcta: MGUS is considered a premyeloma state and carries roughly a 1-2% per year risk of transforming into multiple myeloma (or a closely related plasma cell/lymphoplasmacytic malignancy). This steady annual risk is why patients with MGUS require ongoing surveillance rather than a one-time evaluation.

incorrectas.B: Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid malignancy of Reed-Sternberg cells and is not the neoplasm that arises from clonal plasma cells in MGUS.
incorrectas.C: Chronic myeloid leukemia is a myeloproliferative disorder driven by the BCR-ABL fusion, unrelated to the plasma cell clone underlying MGUS progression.
incorrectas.D: Aplastic anemia is marrow failure with pancytopenia and a hypocellular marrow, not a clonal plasma cell malignancy that MGUS evolves into.

preguntas.q: A B-cell lymphoma characterized by monoclonal IgM production and generalized lymphadenopathy, without lytic bone lesions, is known as:

e.correcta: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia is a lymphoplasmacytic (B-cell) lymphoma that secretes a monoclonal IgM. The large, pentameric IgM molecule raises serum viscosity, producing hyperviscosity symptoms such as visual disturbances, headache, and mucosal bleeding, while notably lacking the lytic bone lesions seen in myeloma.

incorrectas.A: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell malignancy that typically produces monoclonal IgG or IgA and causes lytic bone lesions and hypercalcemia, rather than the IgM and hyperviscosity picture of Waldenstrom.
incorrectas.C: MGUS is an asymptomatic monoclonal gammopathy with an M spike but without the tissue infiltration, lymphadenopathy, or IgM-driven hyperviscosity that define Waldenstrom.
incorrectas.D: Burkitt lymphoma is an aggressive B-cell lymphoma associated with c-myc translocation and a starry-sky histology; it does not secrete a monoclonal IgM paraprotein.

preguntas.q: A 68-year-old man has a monoclonal IgM spike, generalized lymphadenopathy, and hyperviscosity symptoms. A skeletal survey is performed. Which finding is characteristically ABSENT in Waldenström macroglobulinemia, helping distinguish it from multiple myeloma?

e.correcta: Waldenström macroglobulinemia is a lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma that secretes monoclonal IgM but, unlike multiple myeloma, does NOT produce lytic bone lesions and lacks the classic CRAB features (hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia from marrow replacement, Bone lesions). The malignant cells infiltrate marrow and lymphoid tissue and flood the serum with bulky IgM pentamers rather than driving osteoclastic bone destruction. Remembering 'no CRAB, no lytic lesions' is the fastest way to separate it from myeloma on a boards vignette.

incorrectas.B: A serum monoclonal (M) spike IS present in Waldenström — it is the defining IgM paraprotein — so this feature does not distinguish it from myeloma and is not absent.
incorrectas.C: Lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of the bone marrow is the characteristic histologic finding in Waldenström, not something that is absent; the malignant cells are a hybrid of lymphocytes and plasma cells.
incorrectas.D: Elevated serum viscosity is a hallmark of Waldenström because the large IgM pentamer thickens the blood; it is present, not absent, and is the source of many of its symptoms.

preguntas.q: A patient with Waldenström macroglobulinemia develops blurred vision, headache, and Raynaud phenomenon. These findings are best explained by which consequence of the monoclonal IgM?

e.correcta: IgM is secreted as a large pentamer, and in Waldenström the massive quantity of circulating IgM dramatically raises serum viscosity. This sludging of blood impairs microcirculation, producing visual disturbances (retinal vein engorgement), headache, dizziness, and cold-induced Raynaud phenomenon. Hyperviscosity is the signature clinical problem of Waldenström and is treated acutely by physically removing the IgM.

incorrectas.B: Hemolysis of red cells causes anemia and jaundice but does not explain the neurologic and visual symptoms of sludged microvasculature; IgM cold agglutinins can cause hemolysis, but the classic triad here reflects viscosity, not red-cell lysis.
incorrectas.C: Amyloid deposition (as in AL amyloidosis from light chains) causes organ infiltration such as cardiomyopathy or nephrotic syndrome, not the acute reversible hyperviscosity syndrome described here.
incorrectas.D: Osteoclast activation drives the lytic bone lesions and hypercalcemia of multiple myeloma — a feature specifically absent in Waldenström — and would not produce visual or Raynaud symptoms.

preguntas.q: A patient with Waldenström macroglobulinemia and very high serum IgM presents with mucosal bleeding and easy bruising despite a normal platelet count. What is the most likely mechanism of the bleeding?

o.A: Defective platelet aggregation from the viscous, protein-coated serum
o.B: Consumption of clotting factors in disseminated intravascular coagulation
o.D: Vitamin K deficiency impairing factor synthesis

e.correcta: The enormous concentration of IgM coats platelets and clotting factors and increases serum viscosity, physically interfering with normal platelet aggregation and interaction with the vessel wall. This produces a qualitative platelet dysfunction and mucocutaneous bleeding even though the platelet count is normal. It is another downstream consequence of the same hyperviscosity that drives the neurologic symptoms.

incorrectas.B: DIC consumes fibrinogen and platelets and would show a low platelet count, elevated D-dimer, and schistocytes — none of which fit an isolated qualitative defect from paraprotein coating.
incorrectas.C: Acquired factor VIII inhibitors cause a prolonged aPTT that does not correct with mixing studies and produce deep hematomas, a mechanism unrelated to the IgM paraprotein's coating effect on platelets.
incorrectas.D: Vitamin K deficiency impairs synthesis of factors II, VII, IX, and X and prolongs the PT/INR, but it does not explain bleeding in the setting of a normal platelet count and a monoclonal IgM.

preguntas.q: A patient with Waldenström macroglobulinemia presents to the emergency department with confusion, blurred vision, and mucosal bleeding from acute hyperviscosity. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

e.correcta: Acute hyperviscosity syndrome is a medical emergency, and plasmapheresis rapidly removes the offending IgM from the serum, since the large pentamer is confined largely to the intravascular space and is efficiently extracted. This immediately lowers viscosity and reverses the visual, neurologic, and bleeding manifestations while definitive chemotherapy against the underlying lymphoma is arranged. Think 'big IgM in the blood → filter it out.'

incorrectas.B: Transfusing red cells actually adds cellular mass and can WORSEN hyperviscosity; it addresses anemia, not the acute viscosity crisis, and is relatively contraindicated before the IgM is removed.
incorrectas.C: Corticosteroids are used in various plasma cell and autoimmune disorders but do not rapidly remove circulating IgM, so they cannot reverse an acute hyperviscosity emergency in the immediate term.
incorrectas.D: Bisphosphonates treat the lytic bone lesions and hypercalcemia of multiple myeloma — problems that do not occur in Waldenström — and have no role in relieving hyperviscosity.

preguntas.q: Langerhans cells, the professional antigen-presenting cells resident in the epidermis, are a specialized subtype of which cell?

e.correcta: Langerhans cells are specialized dendritic cells that reside predominantly in the skin, where they capture antigen and migrate to lymph nodes to prime naive T cells. As professional antigen-presenting cells they express abundant MHC class II and are highly efficient at initiating adaptive immune responses. Their skin location makes them the immune system's first sentinel against cutaneous pathogens.

incorrectas.B: Mast cells are granulocyte-lineage cells loaded with histamine that drive type I hypersensitivity and allergic responses; they are not professional antigen-presenting cells like Langerhans cells.
incorrectas.C: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated B cells that secrete antibody and do not present antigen to naive T cells, so they are functionally distinct from dendritic Langerhans cells.
incorrectas.D: Natural killer cells are innate lymphocytes that kill virus-infected and stressed cells via perforin and granzyme; they are effectors, not the antigen-presenting dendritic cells found in skin.

preguntas.q: The dendritic Langerhans cells of the epidermis originate from which bone marrow precursor?

e.correcta: Langerhans cells are derived from bone marrow monocytes, which seed the epidermis and differentiate into resident dendritic antigen-presenting cells. This monocyte/macrophage lineage origin explains why they share markers such as S100 and CD1a with other cells of the mononuclear phagocyte system. Recognizing their myelomonocytic origin helps explain why Langerhans cell histiocytosis behaves as a proliferation of these dendritic cells.

incorrectas.B: Granulocytic myeloblasts give rise to neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils, not to tissue dendritic cells; Langerhans cells arise from the monocyte branch of the myeloid lineage instead.
incorrectas.C: The common lymphoid progenitor produces T cells, B cells, and NK cells; Langerhans cells are of myelomonocytic (monocyte) origin, not lymphoid.
incorrectas.D: Megakaryocytes are the giant marrow cells that shed platelets and have no role in generating antigen-presenting dendritic cells of the skin.

preguntas.q: After capturing antigen in the skin and migrating to a lymph node, Langerhans cells present that antigen to prime which type of naive lymphocyte?

e.correcta: As professional antigen-presenting cells, Langerhans cells display processed antigen on MHC molecules and travel to regional lymph nodes to present it to naive T cells, initiating the adaptive immune response. This priming of T cells in the paracortex is the central job of dendritic cells. Their loss of function when they become neoplastic is one reason Langerhans cell histiocytosis cells are considered functionally immature.

incorrectas.B: Naive B cells are activated primarily by antigen binding their surface immunoglobulin plus helper T-cell signals; dendritic cells classically prime T cells rather than directly presenting to naive B cells.
